544570|2026-09.headline: WeWork India Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31.6% YoY to INR768.7 crore and EBITDA margin reached 21.2%, with PAT up 67.4% to INR65.8 crore.
544570|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was a strong quarter: revenue grew 31.6% YoY and 10.1% QoQ to about INR768.7 crore, and EBITDA rose 37.6% YoY to INR162.9 crore at a 21.2% margin. The company added a record ~11,700 desks in the quarter, taking capacity to 145,300 desks across 85 centres, while occupancy rose 357 bps YoY to 83.7%. Net debt of INR310 crore a year ago turned into net cash of INR23 crore, and ROCE reached 34.5%. Management guided to 150,000-155,000 desks by March 2027, and the company is laying out a 190,000-200,000 seat path. All figures are on an IGAAP-equivalent basis.

segments.name: Core flex / membership
segments.commentary: Core business revenue INR657.7 crore, up 31.7% YoY. Members grew 32.5% to about 121,700, and occupancy reached 83.7% (mature centres ~88%, growth centres 64.8% vs 51.4% a year ago).

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: VAS revenue INR79.6 crore, up 35% YoY; management says VAS is margin accretive. Customization revenue about INR18 crore in Q2 and about INR30 crore in H1, with flow-through to EBITDA.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Digital revenue INR29.2 crore, up 46% YoY, operating at close to 80% EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: Desk count expected at about 150,000-155,000 by March 2027 (145,300 at Sept 30; ~4,500 added by Oct 5, so already ~150,000); some March deliveries could slip to early April.
Longer term: path to about 190,000-200,000 seats, with FY28 and FY29 supply under negotiation; management says FY28 rollout will be higher than FY27.
Margins: Q3 and Q4 to see further expansion as occupancy rises, with larger step-up in Q4 as rent freezes expire; capacity additions lower in the next two quarters.
FY27 capex about INR500-odd crore for the full year (H2 lower than H1's INR363.8 crore, though one large deal adds capex). FY28 capex likely near INR600 crore or slightly more.
FCFO-to-EBITDA conversion expected in a 1.2x-1.5x range.
PAT margin hovering in 7%-10% range going forward; EBITDA margin range of 20%-23% for next year, depending on capacity timing.
Largest-ever deal to be announced next quarter; expected to require significant capex on a single asset.
capex_capacity: Desks at 145,300 across 85 centres in 8 cities (+27% YoY); ~11,700 desks added in Q2 (record), ~18,400 in H1, ~4,500 more in October.
Bengaluru 54,000 desks (anchor); Hyderabad 20,000 (now second-largest, overtook Mumbai); Pune 17,000.
Q2 additions: Chennai ~3,600 desks (managed office extension), Hyderabad ~2,700 (WeWork-branded), Pune ~2,600 (managed offices).

Pipeline: 9,000+ desks under signed leases and fit-out, ~38,000 seats under LOI; total ~47,000 incremental seats (32% above current capacity). Management cites a further ~2 million sq ft of prospective space not yet at LOI stage.
Growth centres (open <12 months) hold ~25,000 desks; portfolio breakeven occupancy 55.7%. Refurbishment cycles expected around year 5-7 per asset.
demand_pricing: Revenue-to-rent multiple at an all-time high of 2.7x; new large managed-office deals are at about 3x, driven by higher capex per sq ft.
Contracted escalations of 6%-7% on existing contracts; renewal rate about 80%-85% in H1 FY27; churn lower than expected.
Average commitment term rose to about 28 months (larger accounts ~32 months).
Locked-in core revenue grew ~66% to INR3,843 crore against INR1,421 crore of rent, about 2.7x coverage (management also cites ~2.9x in Q&A).
Enterprises 77% of core revenue; GCCs ~41% of mix; other global companies ~26%; Fortune 500 ~30%; top 10 members 23% of revenue.
Minimum wage increases in Karnataka near 60% and backdated BESCOM energy tariffs pressured opex per sq ft in H1; management says margin would be ~22%-23% without these.

qa_highlights.question: How has underwriting changed for new centres (payback, revenue-to-rent) given rising competition and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is taking larger positions in Grade A assets, underwriting buildings under development, and doing multi-property deals; it says underwriting is smarter but not drastically changed versus two years ago. Payback periods are improving and capex control is driving better returns.

qa_highlights.question: Renewal trends and pricing on renewals versus new contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal rate 80%-85% in H1; renewal escalations are lower than contracted escalations and pricing on fill-up, as management trades price for loyalty and scale. Around 50% of customer growth comes from existing members expanding.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation between expansion and FCF, and use of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: More FY28 expansion is planned with additional capex; the company is also looking at buybacks or dividends once book losses are cleared, and at investing in adjacent businesses that help Indian companies scale.

qa_highlights.question: Customization revenue in Q2 and EBITDA flow-through; GCC hiring outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Customization was about INR18 crore in Q2 and about INR30 crore in H1, with flow-through to EBITDA; management says large lumpiness is normalised. Management sees GCCs continuing to set up in India and expects demand to grow, with premium managed offices and more amenities.

qa_highlights.question: Will March 2027 desk target of 155,000 be met, and what H2 margin uplift to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Already at about 150,000 desks; 155,000 visibility by March, though some deliveries may slip into early April. Margins to expand further in Q3 and Q4, with the larger step-up in Q4 as rent freezes expire. Q4 YoY margin change expected to be modest given a strong Q4 last year.

qa_highlights.question: Margin guidance for next year and pipeline beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise percentage guidance; FY28 EBITDA margin range of 20%-23%, depending on capacity timing. Pipeline: about 2 million sq ft of additional prospective space not yet signed; leases signed about 12 months out with ~95% visibility, 70%-80% at 18-24 months.

risks_watch: Opex inflation: Karnataka minimum wage hikes near 60% and BESCOM backdated energy tariffs; margin outlook depends on it.
Depreciation rising with the largest capex cycle; PAT margin guided at 7%-10%.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia (~1.2 million sq ft built-to-suit campus in Manyata, a customer for ~7 years) is expected to move out; timing uncertain. Another possible lumpy move-out next year.
Promoter pledge still outstanding; management says it will reduce it over time, with no block sale at current prices, and has three years to repay the debt.
Capex upside risk if more managed-office deals are signed; one very large deal to be announced next quarter.
Desk target of 155,000 by March 2027 could slip into early April.
544570|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and detailed on demand, occupancy, margins and cash generation. Cautious on forward margin and capex numbers, with ranges given and direct refusals to guide a single percentage. Evasive on the promoter pledge timing, saying it will come down only when pricing makes sense.
key_quotes: Demand is keeping pace with our largest openings. Our platform is compounding beyond the desk, and margins, returns, and cash, all strengthening throughout the build.
Locked-in core revenue grew nearly 66% to about INR3,843 crores, covering the INR1,421 crores of rent locked in against it, which is about 2.7 times.

We are in no hurry to close it, because we have three years to basically sort of like pay that debt off, and clearly the business is growing faster than the cost of capital that we have for that debt.
So, capex would possibly be closer to the INR600 crores mark, or maybe even slightly more than that for FY28.

544572|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 sales rose 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion; reported PBT margin 9.5%, or 11.5% excluding demerger one-offs.
544572|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 (Jan–Mar 2026) revenue grew 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion, led by OEM orders from wind, metals and rail. Reported PBT margin recovered to 9.5% from negative 7.8% in Q3, but this includes demerger-related one-offs; excluding them, margin was 11.5% versus 13.1% in Q3. Net working capital fell 2.8% QoQ to 18.7% of sales on lower inventory. Management guided margins back to around 13% after demerger costs end and about 15% by FY29-30, with capex of around INR 800 crore planned through FY30 for a new Pune plant. YoY comparisons were not presented because prior-period figures were extracted from SKF India Limited.

from -7.8% in Q3 FY26; +1,731 bps QoQ

segments.name: OEM

segments.name: Distribution

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports performed well in Q4, mainly to Europe and Southeast Asia; about 6% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Sales to SKF India (automotive)
segments.commentary: Intercompany sales to SKF India Limited were the second-largest growth driver in Q4, linked to automotive demand; about 4% of FY26 revenue.

guidance_outlook: Margin (excl. one-offs) expected to return to around 13% by end of calendar 2026 as demerger costs finish and distribution mix recovers.
Long-term target of about 15% PBT margin by FY29-30, with 16-18% as aspiration but not committed.
Net working capital expected at 19-20% of sales going forward.
Growth expected around 8% in the interim until the new Pune plant is operational.
Expect to pass on FX impact and 3-4% cost escalation through price increases; pricing actions already taken with distributors.
capex_capacity: Total capex of around INR 800 crore plus over FY26 to FY30, mainly for the new Pune plant and new DGBB and TRB channels.
New Pune plant expected to start operating mid-2028, with full channel transfer and ramp-up complete by end of calendar 2028.
Tapered roller bearing capacity at Pune raised from 600,000 to 886,000 pieces via machine upgrades; cost down about 18%, changeover time down 20%, new product lead time down about 35%.
Until the new plant is ready, SKF India Limited continues job-work manufacturing; additional demand sourced from SKF Ahmedabad and Nilai.
demand_pricing: Industrial production grew about 4.5% YoY; construction grew 6.6% and iron and steel production 9.7%.
Wind is primarily India-driven; India is described as the fastest-growing wind market. Company exited wind and some rail (freight) and tractor business earlier and is re-entering due to localization.
Q4 margin was pressured by OEM mix (lower margin) and higher employee cost from full 100% bonus accrual versus partial payout in Q3.

Other expenses rose on royalty and trademark payments (about INR 60 million higher) and manufacturing costs (repairs, power and fuel, stores). A transfer pricing margin on services from SKF India was also booked.
Competition described as intense, especially at OEMs. Rupee depreciation is a bigger cost headwind than steel and oil-linked inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 segment-wise mix across general machinery, heavy industries, metals, railway, wind, OEM, aftermarket and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26: distribution about 35%, OEM about 51%, exports about 6%, SKF India sales about 4%, other income about 3%. Within OEM: railway 11%, general machinery 7%, wind and defence 7%, heavy industries 7%, metals 6%.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation trending, how much price has been taken, and how will margins evolve with capacity additions and demerger costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin to return to about 13% by end of calendar 2026; about 15% by FY29-30. Cost escalation projected at 3-4%, with FX as the bigger headwind. Pricing actions already taken with distributors; OEM price escalation being negotiated and expected to be harder.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gap between current margins and the 13-15% historical range, and what drives the path to 16-18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Drags are extra investments in Pune including the new plant, intense OEM competition, higher railway mix, and higher depreciation. Management targets around 15% through 2030 and says 16-18% is an aspiration that cannot yet be committed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company prioritise growth over margin, given exits and re-entries in wind, rail and tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy is growth while maintaining margin, with a target of about 15%. Re-entering wind, freight rail and tractor segments through localization means winning share at lower OEM margins, which management expects to improve through efficiency and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex timeline and when will new capacity be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of around INR 800 crore plus over FY26 to FY30. New Pune plant expected to be operational mid-2028, with full ramp-up and channel transfers complete by end of 2028.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 350-400 crore channel expansion investment and how will growth be delivered until the new plant is ready?
qa_highlights.answer: The investment is plant and machinery for DGBB and TRB channels at the new Pune plant, not warehouses. Growth is guided at about 8% in the interim, supported by job-work from SKF India and sourcing from Ahmedabad and Nilai.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the demerger cost roll-off, distribution mix recovery, and price pass-through of FX and 3-4% cost escalation, especially with OEM customers.
Rupee depreciation and steel and oil-linked costs could widen the cost gap.
Heavy intercompany activity with SKF India Limited: sales, transfer pricing margin, royalty and payables/receivables settlement could affect working capital.
Distribution volume was held back due to overdue payments; watch whether distributor volumes recover in the next quarters.
Capex execution on the new Pune plant (mid-2028 start, end-2028 full ramp) and any delays.

544572|2026-06.headline: SKF India (Industrial) Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.3% YoY to INR 9,708 mn, but PBT margin fell to ~9% on FX losses and demerger IT costs.
544572|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 9,708 million, up 18.3% YoY (on management's constructed comparison) and 2.6% QoQ. PBT was INR 869 million, a margin of about 9%, hit by roughly INR 147 million of forex loss and about INR 150 million of demerger-related IT separation cost. Operating cash conversion was 63%, with a one-time outflow for name change and land transfer. Management reiterated a long-term PBT margin path of 14-16% through 2028, with a 17-19% aspiration, and a new Pune plant with INR 850-950 crore capex targeted for 2028.

Rupee depreciation, linked to Middle East war; on imports mainly from Europe
Incremental one-time cost in the quarter

guidance_outlook: Long-term PBT margin guidance of 14-16%, described as conservative; aspiration 17-19%, with near-term pressure from investments through 2028.
Management expects demerger IT costs to continue for two more quarters, tapering by end-2026 and ceasing around Q4/Q1 FY28.
Management said ~12% is a fair margin on current performance excluding the one-offs; manufacturing efficiency could add a couple of percentage points more.

One additional TRB channel to be added by early 2027 despite capacity constraints.
Plan to add around 15-20 lines, some transferred from SKF group companies and some new; most depend on the new factory.
Capex plan quoted as INR 900-950 crore in prepared remarks and INR 850-900 crore in later Q&A; figures are inconsistent in the transcript.
demand_pricing: Order book reported as growing, with sustained growth over the last few quarters.
INR 140 crore gearbox-manufacturer order (wind-related, one-year, spread through the year) and INR 35 crore agricultural tractor OEM contract.
Innovation traction strongest in general machinery (gearboxes, motors, pumps); agriculture uses customised offerings.
Data center and humanoid opportunities are early-stage; current data center traction is in basic pumps, with no material revenue yet.
Management said the Indian Automotive sales share is being reduced to improve mix.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the margin moderation from the 16-19% guidance to 14-16%, and how much is FX and demerger impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 14-16% is the conservative long-term path and 17-19% the aspiration; near-term margins dip due to investments. CFO quantified FX plus demerger one-offs at about 3% of margin, implying ~12% underlying.

qa_highlights.question: What is the supply and recurrence profile of the INR 140 crore wind and INR 35 crore agri orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Most orders are one-time or one-year contracts, typically extending one to two years. Some services and condition-monitoring contracts are longer-term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin difference across distribution, OE and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution is the higher-margin channel at high double-digit margins; OE is high single-digit. OE supports aftermarket share growth.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the solutions business and what is the doubling timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Solutions are around 6-7% of India business, below 10% in aspiration. Doubling the business is an aspiration within five years at the outside, with no committed timeline.

qa_highlights.question: When will one-off costs end, and is 12% margin achievable now?
qa_highlights.answer: The IT cost should taper through end-2026 and stop around Q4 FY27/Q1 FY28. CFO said ~12% is a fair current margin, with further gains from efficiency and the Pune plant.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company merge with the SKF automotive or other group entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no active plans; it wants the demerger to stabilise first but continuously evaluates options.

risks_watch: Forex: rupee depreciation linked to Middle East tensions raised import costs on European-sourced products; margin impact depends on INR movement.
Demerger one-offs: IT separation costs of about INR 150 million per quarter expected for two more quarters; watch for taper.
Capacity constraint until the 2028 Pune plant; growth above current capacity is limited, with only one added TRB channel by early 2027.
Execution risk on INR 850-950 crore capex and the 5-7 year payback; management figures varied across the call.
Management transition: Sujeeth Pai takes over as MD on 1 September 2026.

544576|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR80.54 bn (+8.1% YoY) but EBITDA margin fell ~250 bps YoY to 11.7%, with FY27 targeting early double-digit margins.
544576|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was LG Electronics India's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR80.54 bn, up 8.1% YoY, with EBITDA of INR9.45 bn (11.7% margin) and PAT of INR6.93 bn (8.5%). Year-on-year margin compression was attributed to channel promotion spend (~1.1 pp), rupee depreciation (~5.6% YoY, ~1 pp impact), and e-waste compliance cost (~0.2 pp). For FY26, revenue grew 1.0% to INR246.05 bn, EBITDA was INR24.08 bn (9.8%) and PAT INR16.85 bn (6.8%). Management guided FY27 to mid-teen revenue growth and early double-digit EBITDA margins, citing April-May sell-through and recent price hikes.

financial_highlights.change: +8.1% YoY vs INR74.48 bn in Q4 FY25
Margin down ~250 bps YoY; up 7% sequentially

segments.name: Home Appliances & Air Solutions (H&A)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR65.16 bn (+5.7% YoY); FY26 revenue INR181.60 bn. EBIT margin 11.9% in Q4, hit by commodity costs, rupee depreciation and channel investments for new launches. Premium washers, French door refrigerators and 5-star RACs saw higher ASPs.

segments.name: Home Entertainment (HE)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR15.37 bn (+19.6% YoY, +15.9% QoQ); FY26 revenue INR64.44 bn. EBIT margin 13.4% in Q4, after time-bound Cricket World Cup marketing spend. OLED market share 60.0% YTD March 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teen percentage; early double-digit EBITDA margin for full year, better than FY26.
Margin recovery levers: localization (55.2% in FY26, targeted +1 to 2 pp per year), operating leverage, richer mix, scaling AMC and B2B, export growth, and industry price increases.
Export expansion targeted 'very significantly' in FY27; large-capacity refrigerators exported to advanced markets from Q1 FY27; Essential Series exports to 22 countries.

Sri City plant: total investment INR50 bn, funded from internal accruals; compressor line Q3 FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026), RAC line Q4 FY27 (Jan-Mar 2027); washing machine and refrigerator lines to follow in phases.
Management expects ROE and ROCE to improve meaningfully in FY27 as profitability normalizes and Sri City capital starts generating returns.
No immediate plan for further price hikes; monitoring raw material and currency movements.
capex_capacity: Sri City (third factory) total planned investment INR50 bn; about INR6.57 bn deployed to March 2026 (CWIP and capital advances) (INR657 crore per Q&A). Next two years' spend largely planned against the INR5,000 crore total.
Sri City timelines: compressor production Q3 FY27; RAC production Q4 FY27; washing machine and refrigerator lines added thereafter in phases. Hiring for key roles has started.
Pune plant produces premium products: 674 litre and 790 litre side-by-side refrigerators, top freezers (790 litre plus) and front-load washing machines for export.
Sri City expected to double export-capable capacity and improve South India logistics (South India is 38-40% of business).
FY26 capex INR5.51 bn; localization rate 55.2%, up ~1.4 pp YoY.
demand_pricing: Channel: AC channel filled in Q4 (55% of annual AC business falls in Q4); >1 million ACs sold in Q4 FY26; industry entered Q1 FY27 with inventory at last year's levels, but March cold spell slowed sell-out. LG says its inventory was in line with plan and manageable.

Price hikes: RAC increased in two phases (BEE-rating driven, then input cost and FX), about 12-13% per analyst; refrigerators and washing machines also repriced. LG says competitive positioning unchanged and no impact on sales.

New categories: French door refrigerator share rose from 5% to 14% by March 2026 after December 2025 launch; chest freezer (market ~INR3,000 crore, five models coming); fixed-speed RAC entry; dishwashers doubled revenue in FY26 and rank #2.
Essential Series (launched 14 Oct 2025): about 100,000 washing machines sold in Q4 FY26; ~80,000 Essential refrigerators in Q4; ~20,000 sub-1-ton RACs (0.8 ton).
TV: 55-inch and above segment grew 47% and now 49% of business; TV revenue grew 20%+ in Q4.
AC penetration in India cited at ~13%; B2B order inflows from government, corporate and hospitality; ID division hit record quarterly sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue growth of 8% not translate into operating leverage and a YoY margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna said margin fell ~250 bps: channel promotion ~1.1 pp (temporary, to drive sell-out and partner confidence), currency depreciation ~1 pp, and e-waste compliance ~0.2 pp as recycling target rose from 60% to 70%. Price hikes, lower promotions and summer demand are expected to restore margins in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is LG doing differently from peers, and how will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Dongmyung Seo cited export scaling, the recovering B2B business, AMC as a high-margin recurring stream, and new categories. Margin levers: exports (core growth engine), localization (55.2%), and a higher mix of AMC and B2B. Lower oil prices after Middle East stabilisation could also help.

qa_highlights.question: What is the channel inventory now versus the start of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Gurpinder Singh said the AC industry entered Q1 FY27 with inventory at last year's levels, with dealers cautious after a slow March. LG's inventory was aligned with plan, and current high temperatures are easing channel pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Are price hikes enough to protect margins, and are more planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said AC prices were raised in two calibrated phases and that LG was first to move, with competitors following. Similar hikes were made on refrigerators and washers with no volume impact. No immediate further hikes are planned, but the company is monitoring raw materials and FX.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex outlook for FY27 and the Sri City timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna confirmed the Sri City plant is on track: compressor line in Q3 FY27, RAC line in Q4 FY27, and washing machine and refrigerator lines later. About INR657 crore is spent to March 2026, with the full INR5,000 crore to be funded from internal accruals over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Does LG still target doubling exports, and what is the Essential Series response?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna reiterated a very significant export expansion, with premium products to developed markets from Pune and Sri City. Sanjay Chitkara said Essential Series sales were encouraging, with 100,000 washers and 80,000 refrigerators in Q4, and exports are going to 22 countries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook for April-May 2026 and the industry growth comparison?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said ACs are well supported by summer demand and the company expects good growth. He targets strong double-digit to mid-teen growth across all four categories in FY27, but gave no industry growth figures for April-May.

qa_highlights.question: Whether the new categories are for domestic or export use?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said the new categories serve both: chest freezers (five models, market ~INR3,000 crore), fixed-speed RACs, and large refrigerators from Pune, which target new domestic business and global markets.

Return ratios (ROE, ROCE) moderated in FY26 due to high cash balance and H1 headwinds; improvement depends on Sri City returns.

544576|2026-06.headline: LG Electronics India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15.5% to INR72.33 billion and EBITDA margin expanded 110 bps to 12.5%.
544576|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 15.5% YoY to INR72.33 billion, with every key category growing double digits on both volume and value. EBITDA rose 26.2% to INR9.04 billion, with margin up 110 bps YoY to 12.5% on product mix, calibrated price increases and operating leverage. PAT grew 27.2% to INR6.53 billion (8.9% margin). Management highlighted record quarterly exports to over 60 countries, Sri City capex of INR5.88 billion out of INR7.36 billion total, and a fully internally funded plan with no external borrowing.

Investment expected to almost double manufacturing capacity and position India as an export hub; funded entirely by internal accruals with no external debt.
Pune and Greater Noida plants being expanded for new Essential family sizes and premium products.

Government notified quantitative restrictions on compressor imports from 8 May: reciprocating compressors restricted up to 60% and rotary compressors up to 70% (per management, against FY25 levels). Management sees this as positive for cost and share.
TV market share is about 26% and OLED share about 59%; 16 new QNED models and Micro RGB TV launched early in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Latika Chopra (J.P. Morgan): How sustainable is Home Entertainment growth, and how much is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said TV grew about 25% for a second straight quarter, with growth from both volume and value; 55-inch and above grew about 53% and now is about 50% of TV business. He called the growth structural and not seasonal.

qa_highlights.question: Latika Chopra: Export growth, US and Europe contribution, FY27 export target, and export margins versus domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports grew 30% in Q1. Two pillars: premium products to key global markets and Essential Series to Asia, Middle East and Africa. Export margins are better than domestic. No numeric FY27 target was given beyond saying the yearly target will be hit.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavani K (Axis): Key growth drivers for FY27 and long-term growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Soonjoo Seo cited exports scaling, premiumisation across categories (large TVs, French door and side-by-side refrigerators, 8 kg+ washing machines, 5-star inverter ACs), and India's role in the global south strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavani K: What is the impact of the revised compressor import policy, given the Q3 compressor facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaganjeet Singh said the policy is positive: LG has 1 million AC capacity at Greater Noida plus 2 million at Sri City, and 7 million refrigerator capacity at Greater Noida, which is above internal needs. Management expects a cost advantage and share gains in refrigerators and ACs.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade (Nuvama): B2B performance and FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said B2B grew strongly; LED signage had its highest ever quarterly sales; commercial AC is expanding distribution and 2-ton 4-star models. Management is confident of a 20% CAGR, as delivered over FY22 to FY25. No Q1 B2B revenue figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade: How is raw material cost inflation being managed, and what is the Q2 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaganjeet Singh listed localisation (including a resin localised in Q1), flexible local and import sourcing, multiple suppliers, and value engineering. Calibrated price increases are already taken; further action depends on input costs. No Q2 margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Siddharth Bora (Nomura): Category-wise FY27 growth outlook, and is Q1 representative?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said all products grew double digits in Q1 and demand is healthy across segments. TV and washing machines are expected to drive H2 growth. No category growth numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Siddharth Bora: Essential Series volume, revenue contribution, further SKUs and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gurpinderjeet Singh said over 500,000 units were sold in six months, margins are in line with the B2C portfolio, refrigerator range expanded to 225, 251 and 276 litres, and a higher-capacity top loader is planned. No revenue share was given.

qa_highlights.question: Vishal Goel (HSBC): Localisation path from 55% and bottlenecks to 70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna said localisation was 55.2% in the last full year, improving 2-3 pp a year, with a target of 65% over the next 3 to 4 years. Sri City AC compressors and local side-by-side refrigerator production at Pune are key steps.

qa_highlights.question: Vishal Goel: Data-centre cooling readiness and dividend or capital return plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mid-scale data-centre cooling is already live with Multi V and chillers; hyperscale is preliminary, with partner-led routes under evaluation and not a key FY27 driver. Atul Khanna said the dividend was set with capex in mind, funding Sri City from internal accruals, and that the dividend policy will be reviewed as cash generation improves.

544595|2026-03.headline: Orkla India Q4 FY26 revenue from products grew 6.2% and EBITDA hit INR 100 crore at 16% margin, with no PLI income booked for FY26.
544595|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from sales of products grew 6.2% on volume growth of 2.2%, with price increases of roughly 4% starting in the quarter. Excluding Kerala, which was hit by distribution restructuring and LPG-linked HoReCa softness, domestic spices grew 11.1% on 6.5% volume growth. FY26 EBITDA was INR 424 crore (16.9% margin) with no PLI income; excluding PLI, EBITDA grew 12.4%. Management flagged West Asia freight costs, Project BOLT digital investments, and renewed spice inflation as near-term margin pressures.

MTR Karam Gold chili powder and MTR Karam launched for AP and Telangana.

95% of raw materials sourced locally; freight surcharges and packaging/logistics costs rising.
Management said small players were exiting Gulf supply due to freight costs, which helps larger players like Orkla.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the Kerala distribution restructuring weigh, and when did it start?
qa_highlights.answer: Project kicked off in Q4; two of three phases implemented, one more by end-May; impact expected for at least two more quarters, with full completion by 1 January 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What growth to expect from exports given 70% GCC exposure, and is the US tariff issue behind?
qa_highlights.answer: Gulf grew about 11.5%, with double-digit growth in the last two quarters. US softness came from destocking across multiple tariff levels (50% down to 16-17%); the business should normalise once inventories are flushed.

qa_highlights.question: What inflation and blended price increase were taken, and are more planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 price increase roughly 4% (6.2% sales growth less 2.2% volume). Another round is planned for Q1 FY27, calibrated to input costs.

qa_highlights.question: How much of EBITDA growth is structural versus temporary (lower ad spend, mix)?
qa_highlights.answer: Around half of the ~250 bps EBITDA margin gain since FY24 came from raw material price declines; the other half from efficiencies, cost reduction, pricing and mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is digital commerce growth incremental household penetration or channel migration?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: reaching new households, including outside South India, while some migration is seen in Southern metro cities. Market-level split not shared.

qa_highlights.question: Is volume growth tonnage-based, and how does PLI work and what was recognised last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume is absolute tonnage across all categories. PLI (six-year scheme from FY22) was not recognised in FY26 due to CAGR thresholds missed after two years of deflation; FY25 recognised INR 20.5 crore; FY27 is the last year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pure vs blended spices split and the convenience food exposure outside South?
qa_highlights.answer: Pure spices about 26% and blended about 39-40% of revenue. Outside South growth is mainly via digital commerce; Breakfast flatness attributed to two quick-commerce platforms restructuring.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term margin aspiration and can Eastern reach MTR margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given. Management said Eastern margins have improved since its 2021 acquisition, with convenience-food shift and cost programmes expected to lift them further, but gap to MTR remains.

Management attributed the step-up in profit partly to one-time gains from the Piramal Imaging deferred consideration and the Shriram Life stake sale, part of which was used to take markdowns and build buffers. qa_highlights.answer: Management expects consol and Growth NIM to converge in the latter half of FY27. Levers are asset mix (unsecured +400-500 bps, gold) and cost of borrowing, with AA+ benefit of 50-80 bps over about three years.

544599|2026-03.headline: Studds Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR 167.5 crore; FY27 guidance is 17-18% revenue growth with broadly flat EBITDA margin.

For FY26, revenue was INR 634.2 crore (up 8.6%), EBITDA INR 122.2 crore (up 16.4%, margin 19.3%) and PAT INR 82.7 crore (up 18.7%). Management took 8-9% price increases from 1 April 2026 to offset raw material inflation, but expects Q1 FY27 gross margin pressure before recovery. Management also announced Bharat Goyal's elevation to CFO effective 1 July 2026, an ESOP plan, and a dividend of INR 3 per share.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12 million capacity target conservative if unpainted helmets are produced more?

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material inflation and will 8-9% price increases offset it?

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin reach 22% as revenue crosses INR 750 crore?

Marketing spend to rise to INR 30 crore in FY27, which could weigh on operating margins.
Leadership transition: Bharat Goyal becomes CFO from 1 July 2026.

Japan was the strongest market; Middle East had a temporary traffic dip that has recovered to near normal.

guidance_outlook: Net new store additions in FY27 expected to be around FY26 levels (FY26: 542 India, 61 international).
Long-term steady-state pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin unchanged at approximately 25% (India currently 14-15%, about 10 pp runway).
Quarterly margins will vary with store-opening phasing, seasonality and long-term bets; management said it will prioritise long-term value over short-term linearity.
Management urged investors to track trailing 12-month volume growth as the cleanest measure of underlying demand.
Step-up in R&D spend in FY27 for automated eye testing, smart eyewear (B by Lenskart) and AI; FY27 priorities include scaling to 100 million customers.
capex_capacity: FY26 store capex funded 603 net new stores (ops cash flow ₹887 crore), alongside manufacturing investment including the new Hyderabad facility.
Factory floors to move toward near full automation from the current 75%; Bhiwadi centralised facility supports next-day delivery across 78 cities (from 7 cities initially, about 30 later).
Hyderabad plant and Thailand JV cited as structural answers to reduce import dependence.
Remote optometry stores rose 3.7x in a year to 623.
India eyewear units reached 29 million in FY26 (18 million two years earlier); long-term store runway of 4,500 stores in India previously articulated, management said more is possible.
demand_pricing: India same-store sales growth 24% in Q4 (broad-based across Metro, Tier 1, Tier 2); same-pincode sales growth 31%. Management declined to split SSSG into value and volume; it rejected an analyst's estimate of ~10% volume SSS as too low.
Eye tests: 6.8 million globally in Q4 (+45% YoY); India eye tests 6 million (+50%); about half of India eye tests were first-time exams. Gold active members 8.8 million (+29.5%).
Product margin in India held at 64% despite rupee depreciation; management said structural margin gains were offset by currency (RMB 11 to 14 cited as an example).
ASP fluctuations are driven by OPP campaigns (New Lens Replacement, Hustlr) and by upgrades to Own days, Meller, progressives.
International ACP reduction ongoing as markets are integrated into central supply chain; operating leverage seen after scale in Singapore, Dubai and now Japan.
Meller sunglasses out of stock in all markets; launched in 1,000+ India stores, Middle East and Southeast Asia, with Japan next.

qa_highlights.question: What geopolitical, raw material, China-sourcing or market risks should investors monitor?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight and raw material have had no meaningful impact so far; currency is the biggest variable. 42% of business is international and vertical integration has offset rupee-import headwinds. No material demand impact seen in India or abroad; Middle East dip was small and brief.

qa_highlights.question: How was the India gross margin held near 64% in a low-ASP quarter, and does SSSG of ~25% with ~15% price imply ~10% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gains came from vertical integration and process changes, not price increases; OPP campaigns are paired with upgrades to offset margin. Management said the 10% volume estimate was not correct and that volume SSS is meaningfully higher; it does not disclose value/volume split.

qa_highlights.question: How will employee productivity and cost leverage trend, especially internationally?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage came mainly from SSG and volume growth on a fixed cost base. HQ and tech costs were flat as headcount was not added; AI and remote optometry are expected to add more output per person.

qa_highlights.question: Does Tier 2 strength expand the 4,500-store runway and allow faster expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than 4,500 stores are possible; 200+ Tier 2 stores have been added and feed GeoIQ. Metros are also growing (eye tests +45%+) and are the main source of SSG.

qa_highlights.question: How should we think about competition in smart glasses (e.g. Google re-entry)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the category is very early with no clear form-factor winner; it sees Lenskart's role in prescription and distribution of smart glasses and its app/data layer as advantages. Launch focus is on learning, not near-term sales.

qa_highlights.question: How will international margins converge to India's level, and what is the KSA breakeven status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a quarter for reaching 15% international margin; it cited falling ACP and operating leverage after scale. KSA is about two years old and ahead of where UAE was at the same stage; no breakeven date was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will store expansion focus on saturating existing pincodes or entering new ones, and what about cannibalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Site selection is bottom-up using mobility data within a 10-minute travel radius, not pincode-level. Management said stores tripled in many cities while revenue doubled, and that much of SSG came from multi-store pincodes.

qa_highlights.question: Is same-day delivery a near-term target and does the store network become an inventory model?
qa_highlights.answer: No delivery target set; same-day is in experiments in Singapore and some Indian markets. Stores are being used as micro-fulfilment nodes for OTC products and at-home frame trials, which management described as a chemist model rather than a warehouse.

qa_highlights.question: What is Meller's traction and scale target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Meller is ahead of plan, sold out across markets, and is being positioned as a Gentle Monster-type brand for Gen Z. No specific scale target was given.

risks_watch: Rupee depreciation: currency is the largest variable on imported product cost; India product margin held at 64% only because of vertical integration and premiumisation.
Quarterly margin volatility from store-opening phasing and OPP-led ASP dilution; management has deliberately deferred linear margin delivery.
International margin ramp (FY26 7%) depends on scale in newer markets such as KSA, which is not yet at EBITDA breakeven.
Metro eye-test wait times and conversion from eye tests (~50% growth) to eyewear volume (~25%) are open execution items.
Smart-glasses competition (e.g., Google re-entry) and heavy R&D step-up in FY27 may pressure near-term margins.
Middle East demand dip was temporary, but geopolitical disruption remains a stated watch item.
Management did not disclose SSSG split between value and volume, which limits external modelling.
544600|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, margin trajectory and long-term runway, with an explicit preference for long-term value over quarterly linearity. Evasive on quantitative detail: declined to split SSSG into value and volume, gave no timeline for international margin to reach India's level, and gave no KSA breakeven date or same-day delivery target.

We urge investors to track trailing 12-month volume growth as the cleanest measure of underlying market expansion.
Our long-term steady-state EBITDA pre-Ind AS margin expectation remains unchanged to approximately 25%.
The compounding effect of revenue and margin will continue, but we will always prioritize action for long-term value creation over short-term linearity.

544600|2026-06.headline: Lenskart Q1 FY27 revenue grew 34% YoY and PAT rose 182% to ₹228 crore, with India same-store sales growth at 18.3%.
544600|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue up 34% YoY and PAT up 182% to ₹228 crore, against full-year FY26 PAT of about ₹530 crore. India revenue grew 30.7% to ₹1,531 crore with pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin of 15.4%, while International revenue grew 38% to ₹1,203 crore with pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin of 10.6%. Store network expansion was the fastest in company history at 455 net new stores over nine months, and the company framed its growth around densification and entry into unserved pin codes. Figures are on a proforma basis, which matched reported figures for the quarter.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,531 crore (+30.7%); product margin 64.2%; marketing 4.8% of revenue (from 5.7%); SSSG 18.3%, same pin code sales growth 24%; eye tests 63 lakh (+42.7%); eyewear units 82 lakh (+22.8%); 116 net new stores and 50 new cities added.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,203 crore (+38%); product margin 77.1%; eyewear units +37.6%, transacting customers +27.8%, eye tests +20.5%, sunglasses units +58.4%; only 16 net new stores added in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management expects International store additions to accelerate in some markets, but said acceleration is more likely in coming years than this year, pending tech integration.
Management said India can support materially more stores (over 6,100 pin codes unserved; densification allows at least another 3,000 stores; India points past 10,000 stores).
Management said it expects Y-o-Y margin improvement in International through FY27 but declined to guide the full-year margin against Q1, which benefits from seasonal sunglasses sales.
Management said short-term currency headwinds could persist if the currency weakens further; product margin offset is expected to improve with Hyderabad plant and insourcing.
capex_capacity: Q1 store capex ₹75 crore and plant capex ₹132 crore, mainly for the Hyderabad facility.
Remote optometry live in 786 stores (up from 168 at FY25 end).
Self AI eye test entered pilot stores; B by Lenskart live with 80,000+ sign-ups and a few hundred glasses shipping daily.
Manufacturing of branded lenses (Rodenstock, Tokai) in India, with plans to extend to international markets.
demand_pricing: Same store sales growth 18.3% in India vs 16% a year earlier; same pin code sales growth 24% (SPSG corrected to 24.3%).
Store density in 1,517 existing pin codes rose from 1.5 to 1.6 stores over nine months; Bangalore SSSG about 20%.
Launched ₹500 eyewear with lenses and warranty via Hustlr Club; premium lenses above ₹30,000 generating about ₹250 crore annually.
Owndays prescription eyeglasses sales over ₹1,500 crore; China market growing about 13% CAGR cited as reference.
Management said ASP can fluctuate quarter to quarter and that lower price points are more margin accretive in absolute rupees.

qa_highlights.question: Will store expansion from ~2,700 to ~10,000 stores hurt same-store sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said densification has not diluted SSSG; penetration is about 35%, and the company is adding new price bands below ₹1,000 and above ₹10,000. It said eye test volume is the funnel driver and that supply-side engineering is the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin resilience a sign that currency concerns are less elevated?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said a large part of revenue is non-INR, giving a natural hedge; product margin was protected by in-house frame manufacturing, vendor volume discounts and mix, but short-term headwinds could persist if the currency weakens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the biggest long-term constraint to the vision: product, real estate or talent?
qa_highlights.answer: Peyush Bansal said talent, especially engineering talent able to apply data and AI, is the main constraint as the company scales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SSSG, SPSG and NPS moderate, and has NPS recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the NPS dip to confusion over social media communication about policies, said it has been clarified and NPS is back near earlier levels, and said SSSG rose from 16% a year ago to 18%.

qa_highlights.question: What share of eye test customers buy glasses and how many bring outside prescriptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a significant majority of eye test customers buy glasses, immediately or within months; first-time customers convert slower. It did not give a percentage for outside prescriptions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the International Q1 margin a fair guide for full-year FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 International EBITDA margin (post-rent) was about 7%, Q1 benefits from seasonally higher-margin sunglasses, and management aims for Y-o-Y improvement but would not guide the full-year margin.

risks_watch: Currency: product margin benefited from hedging and sourcing actions, but further INR movement could weigh on margins.
Store productivity: rapid store additions could dilute same store sales and NPS; NPS dip was attributed to a policy communication issue.
Conversion risk: rising first-time eye tests may lower conversion from eye tests to purchases, per management.
International expansion pace remains slow (16 net new stores in the quarter), with tech integration gating acceleration.
Talent and engineering capacity flagged by management as the most important constraint to the expansion plan.
Accuracy of remote optometry and self eye test; no defined accuracy metric yet, with exchange-for-power-change tracking as a proxy.

The key here will be supply.
Talent and the culture, the speed of operation.

544602|2026-06.headline: Allcargo Global Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5.8% YoY to INR3,522 crores; EBITDA turned positive at INR33 crores versus a INR31 crore loss a year ago.
544602|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR3,522 crores, up 5.8% YoY and 20.8% QoQ, with gross profit of INR733 crores (up 2.5% YoY, 6.5% QoQ). EBITDA was INR33 crores against a loss of INR31 crores in Q1 FY26 and INR17 crores in Q4 FY26. Losses narrowed at EBIT (loss of INR18 crores) and PAT (loss of INR28 crores), and standalone borrowings fell to INR272 crores from INR314 crores at March 31, 2026. Management attributed the volume recovery to sequential trade-lane improvement after inventory corrections, while the Middle East conflict continued to weigh on FCL volumes.

vs loss of INR87 crores in Q1 FY26; vs loss of INR45 crores in Q4 FY26

segments.name: LCL (less than container load)
segments.commentary: Mainstay and highest-margin business; about 14.5% global market share. Volumes up about 5% QoQ, but down about 4% YoY and about 10% below levels of two years ago.

segments.name: FCL (full container load)
segments.commentary: Volumes up about 1% QoQ and down double digits YoY, weighed by Middle East exposure. FCL market share is under 1%.

segments.name: Air freight
segments.commentary: Volumes up about 5% QoQ; double-digit YoY decline per management. Smaller part of the business.

guidance_outlook: Base case assumes no substantial volume growth; management expects marginal monthly volume uptick over the next few months, in line with typical seasonality.
Intent is to keep cost flat in USD terms over the coming couple of years, including employee and admin expenses.
Management expects marginal incremental profit improvement, with gross profit per unit (yield) expected to hold at current levels.
Ballpark of 12% to 15% volume growth from current levels needed to reach desired profitability trajectory; part from market share, part from trade rebound.
Net debt expected to fall significantly over the next two to three quarters via working capital reduction and non-core asset sales; update promised in coming quarter.
No guidance on return on capital employed, though management said it should return to the historical 'north of 20%' zone broadly.
capex_capacity: Business described as asset-light with minimal owned capital assets; capex a tiny fraction of P&L.
Non-core divestments: warehousing and office assets, combined about USD10 million to USD15 million.
Network optimisation: loss-making trade lanes reduced; focus on container utilisation.
Cost initiatives: AI/agentic automation, offshoring to lower-cost geographies, single global system for finance, HR and operations.
Management said no further acquisitions needed near term; growth to come organically by hiring teams for new products and markets.
demand_pricing: Volume growth in Q1 was about half market growth and half market outperformance, per management.
Middle East conflict has depressed volumes for about 5 to 6 months; inventory corrections drove momentum on transatlantic, transpacific and intra-Asia lanes.
Carrier capacity constrained by disruptions, keeping freight rates elevated; management said freight rates rose about 20% to 30% (per analyst question) and is passed through in revenue and costs.
Gross profit growth of about 6.6% QoQ versus about 4.1% implied by volume mix; management attributed the extra 2 to 2.5% to freight environment and efficiencies.
Industry volumes down about 13% to 14% over last two years; Allcargo outperforming by about 3% to 4%. Growth in Latin America, Southeast Asia and India offset declines in Europe and US.

qa_highlights.question: Is the industry cyclical and why have yields fallen since FY24?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the post-COVID 21 to 24 month period was exceptional for FCL margins, and excluding it yield has improved continuously; volumes, not yields, have been the drag. It described the business as shadowing trade conditions rather than cycling.

qa_highlights.question: Why are volumes declining when global trade is broadly flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LCL has declined more than the industry on a YoY basis, while FCL decline is higher for Allcargo due to Middle East exposure. No alternative to LCL exists except air for small shipments averaging 3 to 4 cubic metres.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost base and is it flat in USD?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is to keep cost flat in USD terms; about 80 to 85% of business sits outside India and ocean freight is the largest cost in USD. Rupee translation affects both revenue and cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt composition and net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is mainly working capital plus acquisition funding. Consolidated gross debt about INR942 crores and net debt about INR570 crores at June quarter-end.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA and ROCE normalisation path is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: No EBITDA margin guidance, since margins are not a relevant metric in this business. Management said ROCE was historically above 20% and should return there broadly; a 12% to 15% volume increase from current levels is the ballpark needed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Near term, no; management said the strategy is to grow by investing in people rather than buying businesses, as all key markets and products are already covered.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict continuing to depress FCL volumes, particularly in and out of the region, with knock-on impact on North Asia.
LCL volumes still about 4% below last year and about 10% below two years ago; no guidance for substantial growth.
Rupee translation and USD cost base: management intends flat USD cost, but reported INR figures will move with exchange rate.
Net debt reduction targeted over two to three quarters depends on working capital release and divestments; still to be evidenced.
Company does not provide gross or EBITDA margin guidance; a monthly yield trend update (indexed, not absolute) is promised from this month.
PAT still negative (loss of INR28 crores); profitability relies on volume recovery and cost discipline.

DITP India growth was 20-25%, while the reported 4% DITP GTV growth was driven by bill payments with one client moving transactions in-house.

544606|2026-09.headline: Pine Labs Q2 FY27 revenue grew about 24% YoY and adjusted EBITDA about 27%; management now expects FY27 revenue growth above 23-23.5%.
544606|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as strong execution, with revenue up about 24% YoY and adjusted EBITDA up about 27%. Management said each business line (offline, issuing, online) grew faster than the market and gained share. Flow-based income rose about 25% YoY while UPI volumes grew about 50%. Management plans to add about 10 lakh soundboxes and sales headcount, and said H2 EBITDA should be well above H1 and FY EBITDA margin should be at least 21%. Analysts pressed on EBITDA margin dilution, UPI MDR economics, capex and indirect cost step-ups; management answered most with qualitative explanations and few new numbers.

segments.name: Enterprise offline
segments.commentary: Management said it retained 100% of enterprise accounts with strong net revenue retention and added Tanishq across all stores in Q2.

segments.name: Mid-market offline
segments.commentary: Nearly 100,000 terminals deployed on a trailing 12-month basis; mid-market cohorts (apparel, F&B, duty free, airports) cited as growing about 39-40%.

segments.name: Issuing (prepaid and gift cards)
segments.commentary: Processing share about 80-85%; distribution grew faster than market. NCMC distribution about 1,000 cards per day, Bharat Yatra 25,000-30,000 cards per month; employee tax benefit card due end November/early December.

segments.name: Online and bill payments
segments.commentary: Top four Q-commerce companies use the gateway; one of the largest consumer billers signed up, going live in Q3.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: UAE about 1 lakh transactions per day (Emirates NBD, Wio Bank); close to 1 lakh POS in Malaysia; 50,000 POS in Philippines; present in about 22 countries. Singapore gift card distribution reduced in Q2 after a large retailer exited, with EBITDA impact called immaterial.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected above the 23-23.5% guided at start of year, per CEO closing remarks.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin expected at least 21% (CEO said 'at least 21'), versus 18% in H1 as described by analyst.
H2 EBITDA expected to be much higher than H1; EBITDA expected to keep expanding over time as flow-based income grows.
Working capital guided at 13-15% of top line for full year; Q3 seasonally weaker cash flow expected.
Contribution margin guided at 72-75% overall, with issuing 52-55% and DITP 81-83%.
Effective tax rate declined vs prior quarter; management gave medium to long-term tax guidance (no figures stated).
capex_capacity: About 10 lakh (1 million) additional soundboxes planned to capture UPI transactions at existing merchants; management said soundboxes cost about Rs.500-600 and capex impact is immaterial.
H1 capex about Rs.240 Crore, including about Rs.35 Crore slipped from Q4 FY26 and about Rs.20-25 Crore of advances (vendors now asking about 80% advance versus 20% earlier) due to chip shortages.
Full-service POS deployments continue at natural pace; not part of the 10 lakh soundbox plan.
Capex described as normalising; management expects steady state across the two years after adjusting for these items.
demand_pricing: UPI accounts for about 75-77% of POS transactions; those transactions grew about 68% compounded over last two years; management expects about 70% growth next year.

UPI MDR: 40 bps cited as the headline rate, with about 11 bps retained by acquirer; implementation timing with NPCI, which management said it does not control. Analyst's sensitivity of Rs.80-230 Crore range (from 5-6 bps to full 40 bps on about Rs.4 lakh Crore run-rate) was described as directionally correct, but management said it books income only when received.
Management said no pricing pressure in offline or online; online price increases by peers allowed Pine Labs to gain share.
Management said soundbox pricing will be transaction-based rather than a Rs.125-130 rental, as merchants will not pay both.
Affordability (EMI) growth now broader than CDIT, with non-CDIT volumes rising; October Navratri and Dussehra described as strong, Diwali read pending over about two weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Will India issuing and acquiring growth (about 40%) accelerate in Q3 given festive season timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Navratri and Dussehra were strong and Diwali visibility comes in about two weeks; growth drivers cited were new use cases such as refund wallets and gaming, not seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Does the UPI GTV outlook for FY28 (about 60% growth) rest on the device count plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management tied it to UPI shift on POS (75-77% of transactions) and to 10 lakh additional soundboxes to capture missed UPI volumes at existing merchants.

qa_highlights.question: What is the addressable GMV and take rate under the UPI MDR change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to estimate net take rate, citing commercial negotiations and possible MCC-based pricing; said only volumes were provided.

qa_highlights.question: Why did international revenue mix dip and does it affect profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to a large global retailer's exit from Singapore gift card distribution, a low-margin business; EBITDA impact called immaterial and revenue for Q2 already reflected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin tracking below last year and will guidance be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales hiring pays back over about nine months, and it does not plan to cut EBITDA guidance; expects at least 21% for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex and indirect costs rise in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex overflow from Q4 (about Rs.35 Crore) and Rs.20-25 Crore advances; indirect cost includes cloud and data at 8.5-9% of top line, outsourced field staff, and GFF sponsorship which fell in Q2 this year versus Q3 last year.

qa_highlights.question: How will cash flow and working capital trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 cash flow strong but not to be extrapolated; FY net working capital expected in 13-15% of top line, with Q3 seasonally weaker.

544608|2026-03.headline: Emmvee FY26 revenue rose 116% to INR 5,049 crore and PAT 193% to INR 1,082 crore, with 9.4 GW order book and 6 GW expansion underway.
544608|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first year as a listed company (IPO Nov 2025, INR 2,900 crore raised), with revenue of INR 5,049 crore, EBITDA of INR 1,734 crore (34% margin) and PAT of INR 1,082 crore (21% margin). Module capacity reached 10.3 GW after two 2.5 GW lines were commissioned (May and Dec 2025), and cell utilisation rose to 69.9% for the year and 79% in Q4. Working capital absorbed cash as inventory built up, while the 6 GW integrated cell and module project at Devanahalli is progressing with IREDA's INR 3,306 crore loan sanctioned. Management stated that FY27 will be a year of execution.

segments.name: Modules
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 10.3 GW at March 31, 2026, 100% TOPCon; module utilisation 43% for FY26, affected by Units 5 and 6 running only part-year. Q4 module production about 953 MW per management in Q&A, and G12R modules now in production.

segments.name: Cells
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 2.94 GW; utilisation 69.9% in FY26 (43.3% in FY25), 79% in Q4 and about 85% in March 2026. Management expects a transition from M10 to G12R cells by end of the current quarter.

guidance_outlook: 6 GW integrated cell and module facility at Devanahalli: module line commissioning expected by end of calendar 2026, cell line by end of FY27.
Post-expansion installed capacity targeted at 16.3 GW modules and 8.9 GW cells by end of FY27.
Ingot and wafer facility of about 9 GW in phases: Phase 1 5 GW, Phase 2 4 GW a year later; first facility planned in FY29. Capex guided at INR 600-700 crore per GW.
Next-quarter DCR mix guided at 30-35% of module sales; by around the beginning of FY28 management expects nearly all sold capacity to be DCR.
Current EBITDA spreads on new orders said to be similar to FY26 levels.
IREDA term loan of INR 3,306 crore at 7.95%; about 75-80% expected to be drawn by March 2027, with 15-20% retention spilling into FY28.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex in cash flow about INR 650 crore; gross block rise of about INR 1,000 crore (adjusted for grant) mainly for Units 5 and 6 modules. Land acquisition of about INR 311 crore for the expansion was expensed this year per the Q&A.
Module line commissioning: 2.5 GW in May 2025 and 2.5 GW in Dec 2025 at Sulibele, Bengaluru.
Land at Devanahalli fully paid and in possession; construction started and module line order finalised.
Management cited that module lines typically reach 65-70% utilisation versus 90-95% for cells, which is why module capacity is sized above cell capacity.
Cell capacity at 2.94 GW already built for G12 and line can switch from M10 to G12R through a kit change.
demand_pricing: DCR module price about INR 21-22/W; non-DCR module about INR 14-15/W. Management says DCR pricing is resilient and has not seen upward pressure despite limited domestic cell capacity.
Customer mix cited: IPPs about 40%, C&I about 30% (from prior analyst framing; not contradicted). Average top-10 customer order size rose to 221 MW from 121 MW.

Demand drivers cited: PM-KUSUM (KUSUM-C) and PM Surya Ghar for DCR; ALMM List-2 for cells expected to phase in, with utility projects bid after August 2025 covered; ALMM for IPP demand expected around FY28 or late 2027.
Exports: zero in FY26 and no export orders in the book; management treats exports as upside.
A customer advance of about INR 320 crore received in FY25 was adjusted this year, lowering the customer advance balance. A 4.5 GW cell order has been advanced in full and supply has started.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: why did inventory build up, and will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the build reflects the ramp-up in Q4 (revenue about INR 1,700 crore, versus about INR 1,000 crore in Q1); CFO said FY26 finished-goods change was INR 636 crore and inventory should be held near current levels, with some reduction possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the production-to-revenue gap large (revenue +67% QoQ vs production +30%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales differ from production, realisations move with raw-material prices, and EBITDA per watt is the better measure; it does not disclose sales MW.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 6 GW cell plan 9 GW versus module 7 GW in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said modules run at 65-70% utilisation versus 90-95% for cells, so module capacity is sized higher to match cell output; module is made to order, cell is batch made-to-stock.

qa_highlights.question: What are the timelines and quantum for the wafer/ingot plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Ingot-wafer of about 9 GW in phases, first facility in FY29, capex about INR 600-700 crore per GW.

qa_highlights.answer: Rate 7.95%; nothing drawn yet, first drawdown expected within about a month; 75-80% expected drawn by March 2027.

544608|2026-06.headline: Emmvee Q1 FY27 revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 1,555 crore, EBITDA margin 35%, PAT INR 380 crore (+103% YoY); order book 9.9 GW.
544608|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 1,555 crore (+51% YoY, down QoQ), with EBITDA of INR 548.1 crore (+56% YoY, -4% QoQ) and EBITDA margin of 35% versus 33% in Q4 FY26. PAT was INR 380.3 crore, helped by finance costs falling to INR 11.1 crore from INR 53.1 crore a year earlier. Module and cell production both hit record quarterly levels, with cell utilisation up to 83%, and order book rose to 9.9 GW after 1,484 MW of inflows. Management reiterated stable EBITDA per watt (module about INR 2.5/W, cell INR 6.0-6.5/W) and a 6 GW TOPCon cell and module expansion on schedule.

Module utilisation in base case expected at similar levels (about 45%) in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA per watt trend for DCR and non-DCR modules?
qa_highlights.answer: Both DCR and non-DCR EBITDA spreads were in line with Q4 FY26 and are expected to remain stable.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin per watt trend and DCR mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided on EBITDA per watt: about INR 2.5/W for modules and INR 6.0-6.5/W for cells, similar to Q4. DCR share of sales was over 50%, including both modules and cells; future mix to be more non-DCR but DCR inventories will be used.

qa_highlights.question: Why did raw material cost fall 18-19% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a healthier DCR mix and higher internal cell consumption plus merchant cell sales; said this is mix-dependent and not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory position at quarter end?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 74.25 crore added to finished goods; management expects the strong order book to liquidate inventory, and raw material stock was deliberately raised due to geopolitical risk.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DCR module shortage in Karnataka real and what about run-rate increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Emmvee is equipped for phased ALMM rollout and ALMM List 3 discussions have begun; it expects cell production run-rate to rise further in coming quarters before new capacity arrives.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA per watt benefit from backward integration and utilisation gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the benefit is visible in absolute EBITDA and mix, not in blended per-watt numbers, because of efficiency gains that offset raw material headwinds.

544608|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 45% YoY to INR3,132 crores and PAT 79% to INR762 crores, with EBITDA margin near 35%.

Finance cost fell to about INR9.5 crores from INR55.2 crores a year earlier after IPO-funded debt repayment. Cell output reached 513 MW at 89% effective utilisation, while module output was 952 MW at about 44% utilisation. Order book stood at about 10.4 GW after record inflows of about 1.5 GW in the quarter, and the 6 GW integrated cell and module expansion remains on schedule (module by December 2026, cell by March 2027).

qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR5,500 crores covers both cell and module; hard cost is about INR4,600 crores, with the rest IDC, contingency and working capital margin money (about INR700 crores). Management also cited design, automation and lower silver use as reasons.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold if module prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices may fall somewhat, but margins can be maintained through silver reduction (220 mg to 60-65 mg), the move to G12R and manufacturing efficiency, with savings passed on to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did creditor days fall from 64 in FY26 to 25 in H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is a dynamic outcome of vendor negotiations; lower credit days were accepted in exchange for better prices, which helps COGS.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the largest customer's revenue share rise to 44% in Q2 from 19% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue share shifts quarter to quarter with delivery timelines; sales are backed by substantial advances or LCs, so credit risk is limited.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing depends on operational efficiency, raw material cost and module efficiency, and that EBITDA per watt is the metric it tracks.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said deferral looks extremely unlikely; utility projects bid before August 2025 still need ALMM-II compliance, and about 30% of the order book is non-DCR.

544609|2026-03.headline: PhysicsWallah FY26 revenue rose 35% to INR3,900 crore and pre-Ind AS EBITDA tripled to INR300 crore; FY26 PAT was still negative at INR24 crore.
544609|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first full year after the November 2025 IPO. Revenue from operations reached INR3,900 crore (+35% YoY), with online up 39% and offline up 31%. Q4 revenue was INR919 crore (+51% YoY) and Q4 pre-Ind AS EBITDA was INR9 crore versus negative INR139 crore a year earlier.

544609|2026-06.headline: PhysicsWallah Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,054 crore; pre-Ind AS EBITDA improved to negative INR44 crore, with NEET calendar shift a drag.

Management reiterated full-year FY27 guidance of 30% revenue growth and 100% EBITDA growth, and introduced first-time online/offline segment reporting.

544610|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 34% to INR 143 crore with 82.5% recurring; FY27 target INR 210 crore, with INR 190 crore visibility cited.
544610|2026-03.overview: Workmates reported FY26 revenue of INR 143 crore (up 34%) and PAT of INR 15.92 crore (up 16%, margin 11.1% vs 13%). Margins compressed: gross margin 32.8% vs 33.9% and EBITDA margin 16.2% vs 17.7%, which management attributes to a Dubai contract exit (about INR 4 crore), a gaming client exit (INR 3.5 crore) and about INR 6 crore of added headcount cost. Management set an FY27 revenue target of INR 210 crore (45%+ growth) and entered FY27 with MRR of INR 13.5 crore per month. This was the company's first earnings call since its BSE SME listing.

FY27 PAT guided at about INR 24-25 crore on INR 210 crore revenue; management said PAT margin would be similar to or higher than FY26 margin.
Margin recovery levers: higher AI and security mix, billable utilisation from 84% toward 88%, and operating leverage as new hires reach full productivity.
FY27 target excludes any US or UK turnover. AI expected to be a meaningful contributor in FY27 and the primary growth engine from FY28.
capex_capacity: Manpower cost about INR 16.9-17 crore on about 170 employees (about INR 9-10 lakh per head); FY27 existing-staff cost expected to rise to INR 18.5-19 crore with appraisals plus about INR 1.5 crore of new hires.
Three delivery centres (Kolkata, Bhubaneswar, Hyderabad); nine locations in total. 120+ AWS-certified professionals out of 170+ staff.

IntelliOps AI operations platform onboarded for more than 60% (later stated 65-70%) of customers; management intends to list it on the AWS marketplace.

Enterprise client count rose from 34 to 38; 28 net new clients added; top 20 accounts contributed 73% of revenue; client retention 95%. Management said top-5 concentration has declined.

Management said customers negotiate hard on managed-services and implementation pricing in India, while accepting AWS consumption costs. Hardware prices reportedly doubled or tripled, which management views as a tailwind for cloud migration.

544612|2026-03.headline: FY26 value added revenue rose 12.3% to INR49,180 million with a record 18.8% EBITDA margin; Q4 EBITDA up 17.6% to INR2,573 million.
544612|2026-03.overview: Management reported its best full year yet: FY26 VAR grew 12.3% to INR49,180 million, EBITDA rose 13.5% to INR9,255 million, and EBITDA margin reached a record 18.8% of VAR. Q4 VAR grew 17.5% to INR14,058 million, with EBITDA margin stable at 18.3% despite geopolitical cost pressures. Advanced Ride Technologies drove growth (FY26 up 19.7%), while Clean Air and Powertrain grew only 5.5% for the year. Lifetime order book stood at INR124,000 million at March 31, 2026, with exports and new Clean Air and bearings wins cited as growth drivers.

segments.name: Clean Air and Powertrain Solutions
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR24,296 million, up 5.5% YoY; Q4 INR6,905 million, up 9.9%. Growth tepid due to OEM and within-OEM mix shifts (lower-end SUVs, EV mix at a European OEM), not share loss per management.

segments.name: Advanced Ride Technologies (suspension)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR24,885 million, up 19.7% YoY; Q4 INR7,153 million, up 26%. DCx DaVinci mechanical suspension adopted by a leading Indian OEM for a flagship SUV.

guidance_outlook: Lifetime order book of INR124,000 million gives 100% visibility of FY2028 internal revenue target; management expects double-digit medium-term growth.
Export order book expected to keep growing; current exports are about 5-6% of sales versus a 14-20% share of the order book (as stated).
New West India shock absorber plant (board-approved) expected to take 6-12 months to commission; peak revenue contribution expected mid-2028 to 2029.
Clean Air entry into the largest Indian PV OEM's supplier panel for a Gasoline Particulate Filter; growth expected from late FY27/FY28.
Management expects margins to remain stable going forward.
Addressable Clean Air content from CAFE 3 and BS7 estimated at INR1,300-1,400 crore over the next three to five years.
capex_capacity: Announced capex of about INR1,400 million across the North India Clean Air facility (announced Q3 FY26) and a new greenfield West India Advanced Ride Technologies plant.
FY26 capex was about INR1,150 million.
Bearings business: new plant not yet decided; management is checking whether existing plants can accommodate the new bearings business.
Capex-to-steady-state revenue ratio cited as roughly 1:3.
Localization about 89-90%, management intends to keep it near 90% over the long term.
demand_pricing: Management says the DCx DaVinci suspension has 3-4 OEMs interested, including Indian, Japanese, Korean and European OEMs; it targets about 50% of India's roughly 5-5.5 million PV market.
Conventional mechanical dampers still dominate over 90% of Indian passenger vehicles.
Export drivers cited: technology equalization (BS6.2 with RDE, Euro 6 RDE), China-plus-one sourcing, labour cost advantage and rupee depreciation.

Direct material cost (steel) recovered through quarterly escalator agreements; indirect costs (freight, currency, plastics, rubber, fuel) being recovered through customer negotiations, which management says can be tough.
Management said currency depreciation gives an immediate 15-20% improvement in global competitiveness.

qa_highlights.question: How will exports ramp over the next two to three years, and when will the new plants and bearings orders commission?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are described as middle-ended, with a critical mass around 2028 and ramp starting 2027-28. The West India plant takes 6-12 months to commission; peak around mid-2028 to 2029. Bearings value not yet disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is content per vehicle for commercial vehicle exhaust systems versus passenger vehicles, and how do diesel, petrol, CNG and hybrid differ?
qa_highlights.answer: A commercial exhaust is 3-4x a passenger car system and can reach 10x for tractors with aftertreatment. Diesel carries higher hot-end content. Hybrids can lift content from 1x to 1.5-2x. CNG and hybrid need exhaust systems with no content loss.

qa_highlights.question: Can exports go directly to third-party OEMs or only to Tenneco group entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports go both to Tenneco group entities and to third-party OEMs with group permission, which management frames as partnership, not competition.

qa_highlights.question: Why no two-wheeler suspension or Clean Air two-wheeler presence, and is the CV localization point about Clean Air?

qa_highlights.question: Why did specialty margin fall to 26%?

qa_highlights.question: Scale-up plans for battery materials and land availability?

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of NSS customer issues and the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Largest infant formula customer scaled down Irish operations due to energy crisis; FY27 flattish to single-digit growth. Plan: new sales head expanding outside Ireland and supplying mostly from India; margins similar to core specialty possible in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and steady-state utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up for raw materials and battery business; long-term working capital cycle closer to 150 days. Optimum utilisation 70-75%.

qa_highlights.question: Europe distribution and phosphoric acid sourcing for battery business?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales team built to replace the exited German distributor; no overlap in existing products. No phosphoric acid sourced from China for SAM (FEOC compliance); about 3 other countries plus India supply.
