544619|2026-09.headline: Sudeep Pharma Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to INR196.7 crore with EBITDA margin of 37.2%, a record quarter despite Fortified Rice pause.
544619|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA, with revenue up 21% YoY and 24% QoQ, and EBITDA margin up about 310 bps YoY to 37.2%. Pharma Food Nutrition (PFN) drove growth, rising 57% YoY, while Specialty Ingredients fell 25% YoY after the Government's Fortified Rice programme paused. PAT grew only 11% YoY to INR51.8 crore because of lower other income, a higher effective tax rate of 27%, and new greenfield depreciation. Management guided to positive YoY growth in Specialty Ingredients in Q3 and Q4 and kept the Dahej battery-materials start date of April 2027.

Export share about 65% of revenue (exports up 24% YoY), domestic about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is Specialty Ingredients underlying growth excluding Fortified Rice, and what growth is expected in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fortified Rice was about 20-25% of segment revenue (INR40-50 crore in FY26). Premix was hit by product mix change even though volumes grew. Non-Fortified Rice premix contracts for Q3 and Q4 are expected to largely offset the loss.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Specialty margin fall while PFN margins rose sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to operating leverage: premix, a large contributor, had limited revenue, and NSS was a drag. Q3 and Q4 contracts are expected to carry better margins than the Fortified Rice business they replace.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PFN growth from volume or pricing, and what is the PFN volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came mainly from phosphates (up about 70-80%) and magnesium bisglycinate, which received the maximum capacity allocation in the existing setup. PFN volume grew about 30-35% in Q2 and about 19% in H1.

qa_highlights.question: How will bisglycinate be distributed across customers, and how much of Nandesari capacity can go to it?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of bisglycinate volume will go to larger customers, including two of the largest US tolling manufacturers, and 50% to mid/small customers, to avoid concentration. About 70-80% of the 40% of capacity allocated to other products would go to bisglycinate; the remaining 60% of the greenfield is mainly phosphates and is not easily fungible.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Phase 1 battery capacity is covered by binding offtake agreements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give volume detail today, saying the company would break it out by customer and volume at the next call or within two months. Binding commitments are targeted for Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the battery pricing premium and return profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is set at a slight premium to China, driven by US 45X PFE-compliant supply rules, and capped by competitiveness. Management targets asset turns of about 3x and ROCE similar to the core business, and will not guide EBITDA margin for the battery business.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Phase 1 plant approval needed for Korean customers, and how long does validation take?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant approval for the Dahej site is expected to take 3-6 months because product and process approval is already in place. Management assumes about half a year of FY28 for commercial supply and revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NSS revenue and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is expected to be flat. FY28 growth should be similar to the core business, and the NSS target EBITDA margin is close to 30% after supply chain changes.

544626|2026-03.headline: Exato Technologies FY26 revenue rose about 35% to Rs 168 crore and PAT about 67% to Rs 16.09 crore, with management guiding 50-60% growth for FY27.

Q4 EBITDA margin fell, which management attributed to heavy investment in US and Australia hiring, travel, events and leadership additions. 544632|2026-03.headline: Meesho says logistics disruption in Q2–Q3 FY26 is behind it; Q4 contribution margin exit rate of 4% is the new baseline.
544632|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a strong quarter, with contribution margin up about 170 bps QoQ, of which roughly 110 bps came from lower logistics cost. The 145 bps one-time logistics headwind was concentrated in Q2 and Q3 FY26 and attributed to short-term capacity building during 3PL consolidation around May 2025. Ad revenue as a percentage of NMV rose QoQ, while reported revenue per order looked flat partly due to accounting changes (first-order discounts now netted against revenue) and a higher prepaid mix. Management gave no EBITDA break-even or FCF timing guidance; it pointed to LTM FCF as the guiding metric, and Q4 cash balance fell about INR300 crore, which management partly attributed to tax payments expected to be recovered.

544632|2026-06.headline: Meesho Q1 FY27: management says logistics cost per delivered order fell about ₹1 QoQ, and it guides to ~25% five-year NMV CAGR.
544632|2026-06.overview: Management said fuel and minimum-wage hikes during Q1 FY27 were absorbed, with cost per delivered order down about ₹1 QoQ, and pricing rose at the same time as costs. NMV growth was about 2% QoQ, which management attributed to seasonality (Eid moved from Q1 last year into Q4) and a higher S&M spend base last year, not a change in the core business. Year-on-year AOV fell about 2% versus the roughly 5% annual baseline decline. New initiatives (Kirana Club, a low-cost local grocery logistics network) remain early and capped at about ₹200 crore annual EBITDA burn; Q1 operating loss was about ₹39 crore. The call also covered a GTA structure for middle- and last-mile logistics under VTPL and a Karnataka gig-worker fee, which management says is stayed and immaterial.

544632|2026-09.headline: Meesho Q2 FY27 contribution margin rose to about 6%, driven mainly by logistics efficiencies, with management reinvesting part of the gain into pricing.
544632|2026-09.overview: Management said the contribution margin improvement was led by logistics efficiencies (RTO reduction, higher order density, middle-mile network redesign, Valmo cost gains) rather than ad take-rate. Management cautioned the 6% CM should not be extrapolated, as part of the gain is held back for seller and consumer pricing once server costs normalise. Adjusted EBITDA margin was about minus 1% of NMV, with a quarterly FCF print helped by a roughly INR523 crore working capital release tied to festive-season timing shifting into September. Festive season sales were described as better than expectations, with traffic at all-time highs, though seller-side supply disruptions from crude and Middle East volatility were flagged.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is from ad take-rate versus logistics?
qa_highlights.answer: Logistics was the primary driver, covering RTO, density, network redesign and Valmo efficiency. Ad-rate details were not disclosed separately. There were no specific volume-slab pricing changes from 3PLs this quarter; these typically come in the December quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is growth not being used to keep CM high, and why pass pricing benefit back now?
qa_highlights.answer: Vidit Aatrey said pricing investments pay off over multiple quarters through the flywheel. Passing back CM would not add 10-15% growth immediately, but it makes more categories and sellers viable over the next 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any sign of rising CAC or churn given the ATU growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Vidit said ATU growth partly reflects festive timing. Marketing is reallocated on CAC and LTV, with the same internal hurdle rates, and new-user growth in big cities is nearly as fast as in smaller towns.

qa_highlights.answer: Dhiresh said Q2 server costs were elevated by GPU capacity bought early for the festive season, with normalisation expected by Q4 FY27. Pre-festive marketing spend also front-loaded costs. Long-run fixed cost is targeted at about 3% of NMV.

Management deferred the consumer EBITDA breakeven target, previously Q4 FY27, and is recalibrating the consumer plan, while aerospace is described as on track. segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR4,480m (+44% YoY) with EBITDA INR331m (7% margin); H1 revenue INR8,781m (+48%) with EBITDA INR638m (7% margin), JV EBITDA +47% YoY in H1.

544642|2026-03.headline: Wakefit FY26 revenue rose 17% to INR1,489 crore, but Q4 revenue growth slowed to 13.5% and margins face near-term pressure from raw-material inflation.

Q4 revenue was INR344 crore (+13.5% YoY) with Q4 operating EBITDA at 6.3%, reflecting higher A&P spend and sharp raw-material inflation (polyol, TDI) from February onward. Management took two price increases of about 7-8% each (March and April), said April 2026 growth was better than JFM, and guided to no material margin change in Q1 FY27 versus March exit levels. It also outlined an 80+ net store addition plan for FY27 and a Jumbo store in early FY28.

544644|2026-03.headline: Corona Remedies Q4FY26 revenue rose 20.2% to INR 353 crore and FY26 PAT grew 33% (adjusted INR 199 crore), with Q4 EBITDA margin down ~90bps to 17.6%.
544644|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 revenue was INR 353 crore (+20.2% YoY) and PAT INR 45 crore (+44% YoY), while EBITDA rose 14.4% to INR 62 crore and margin fell about 90bps to 17.6% due to new divisions, MR additions and R&D spend. For FY26, revenue grew 17.3% to INR 1,403 crore, EBITDA rose 22.3% to INR 293 crore (20.9% margin, +80bps), and adjusted PAT grew 33.4% to INR 199 crore after a one-time labour code charge. Management declared a 100% dividend (INR 2 per share) and guided to 15% organic revenue growth, 25% growth on acquired brands and 20%+ PAT growth in FY27.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Grew 29.5% in FY26 and 70% in Q4FY26, but is only ~4% of revenue. Operates on a B2B model with lower gross margin and higher EBITDA than India B2C; management targets high-single to low-double digit growth.

segments.name: Chronic and semi-chronic portfolio
segments.commentary: Contributes 72% of revenue per PharmaTrac MAT March 2026 (71.9% in FY26). Two brands crossed INR 100 crore; two brands are in the INR 100-200 crore club and eight in the INR 50-100 crore club.

segments.commentary: Bayer seven-brand portfolio relaunched in Q4FY26 with an infertility division; Menodac and Fostine R named as focus brands. Wokadine (No. 2 in Indian povidone iodine, ~INR 20 crore revenue) expected to grow ~25% p.a. for 3-4 years with ~400bps gross margin correction in year one.

segments.name: Biosimilars and biologics / Semaglutide
segments.commentary: Three biosimilar launches in FY26 (Fostine R, Tricium DnaB, Wyntide, Tyvenza as named on the call). Semaglutide generics made via MSM as manufacturing partner; Wyntide targets super-specialists and Tyvenza targets tier 2/3 markets.

guidance_outlook: Maintain 15%+ organic revenue growth, 25% growth on acquired brands, and 20%+ PAT growth in FY27 and for the next 2-3 years.
Gross margin expected to be sustained around 80% in coming years, supported by product mix; Middle East/oil-linked API cost risk too early to quantify, with ~90-120 days of inventory on hand.
EBITDA margin expected to improve over time through productivity and operating leverage; management cited 24-25% as a question from an analyst but did not commit to a target.
Expects IPM growth of 10-10.5% in FY27 (volume 1.5-2%), with Corona volume growth of 3x-4x the market.
Bhayla hormone plant and 600-kg line expansion to become operational in Q1 or Q2 FY27; European and Eurasian market revenue expected to build over 2-3 years.
Management says the 15% revenue and 20% PAT framework is unchanged for international business; international expected at 8-9% CAGR over the next 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Dedicated hormone manufacturing plant (Bhayla) expected operational in Q1 or Q2 FY27; new 600-kg line expansion under way.

MR strength at 3,100 after adding ~450 in FY26 (2,630 prior base); management says it is comfortable with current MR strength for FY27.

PharmaTrac pricing growth reported at ~7.8% per management slide; management attributes this to 92-93% non-NLEM portfolio, with volume outgrowing price.
PCPM rose to INR 4.11 lakh per month from INR 3.62 lakh a year earlier; MR tenure buckets targeted at INR 2 lakh (0-3 yrs), INR 4 lakh (3-6 yrs), INR 6-8 lakh (6+ yrs).
Advertising plus sales promotion ~19% of FY26 sales: ~10% KOL consulting, ~5% S&D promotion, ~4% scientific conferences.
Raw material imports under 1% of RM, so limited direct FX/import exposure; indirect cost pressure from API makers.
Semaglutide first-year India market estimated by management at INR 2,000-2,500 crore (range quoted by analysts INR 500-5,000 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Is 17-18% the right EBITDA margin range, or is 20%+ achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 margin dip reflected MR and employee additions; FY26 margin was 20.9% (+80bps), and it expects productivity-led improvement, with current MR strength considered sufficient for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of Q4 margin dip and whether Q4 seasonality is structural?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 9 crore employee cost for two new divisions and MRs, INR 5 crore MR allowances in other expenses and INR 1.6 crore R&D (BE) cost; management cited seasonality plus the two new divisions and asked analysts to look at H1 vs H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~7.8% pricing growth sustainable and what is the Middle East impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing is sustainable given 92-93% non-NLEM exposure; too early to quantify Middle East/oil impact on gross margin, with 90-120 days of inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What are PCPM, export margin profile and AI use in doctor engagement?
qa_highlights.answer: PCPM is INR 4.11 lakh (vs INR 3.62 lakh); exports carry lower gross margin and higher EBITDA margin under B2B; AI is used in the SFE tool for reps and a diagnosis/prescription tool for doctors.

qa_highlights.question: How will Wokadine and the Bayer brands scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Wokadine expected to grow ~25% for 3-4 years with ~400bps gross margin correction in year one, shifting focus to non-NLEM SKUs; Menodac and Fostine R are the Bayer arrowhead brands, with a target of INR 50-100 crore over the next few years.

qa_highlights.question: Is IPM acceleration sustainable and will volume outperformance hold?

API and crude-linked raw material inflation (Middle East) could pressure the ~80% gross margin; management flagged 90-120 days of inventory cover.
Wokadine gross margin correction of ~400bps in year one and possible further 600-700bps; Bayer infertility relaunch progress to be reviewed in 3-4 months.
Semaglutide market size estimates vary widely (INR 500-5,000 crore), and clarity is expected in 2-3 months.
Short-term borrowings of INR 143 crore are overdraft against FDs (net cash ~INR 15 crore) linked to the Wokadine acquisition; a INR 16 crore Myoril loan is to be repaid in FY27.
Export ramp-up depends on 1.5-2 years per country registration; international growth expected at 8-9% CAGR, so near-term contribution stays small.

key_quotes: Our philosophy is to grow 15% on a revenue and 20% on a PAT basis on a year-on-year basis for coming 3 to 5 years down the line.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bayer seven-brand portfolio relaunched in Q4 FY26 with an infertility division (Menodac and Fostine R as focus brands targeting INR 50-100 crore), and Semaglutide generics via MSM partner with a INR 2,000-2,500 crore first-year market estimate, though analysts' range is INR 500-5,000 crore.

rows.why: EAEU GMP certification received for Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Armenia and Kyrgyzstan and Bhayla is EU-approved, but 1.5-2 years per country registration and international is only ~4% of revenue growing 8-9% CAGR.

rows.label: Pricing sustainability on non-NLEM mix

544644|2026-06.headline: Corona Remedies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21.9% YoY to INR422 crore, with EBITDA margin up ~190 bps to 22%.
544644|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 21.9% YoY to INR422 crore, with India business up 22.7% against IPM growth of 11.6%, and organic growth of 21.4%. EBITDA rose 33.5% to INR93 crore and PAT rose 30.1% to INR60 crore, with PAT margin at 14.2%. Management kept FY27 guidance of 15% organic revenue growth and 20% PAT growth, but flagged raw material and geopolitical cost risk and said it is premature to extrapolate the Q1 margin. The Europe-GMP hormonal facility was capitalised on 30 June 2026 and export filings are targeted for FY28-29.

financial_highlights.change: +21.9% YoY (vs INR347 crore in Q1 FY26)
+33.5% YoY; margin up ~190 bps (from INR70 crore)
vs INR10 crore in Q1 FY26; mainly amortisation of Wokadine and Bayer brands

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Contributed about 97% of revenue and grew 22.7% YoY, roughly twice the IPM growth of 11.6%.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Contributed about 3% of revenue and did not grow in Q1; management says it will stay in the low-single-digit share for the next few years.

segments.name: Therapy areas (PharmaTrac, per management)
segments.commentary: Women's Healthcare grew about 23.3% vs IPM 9.4%; Urology grew 27.6% vs IPM 14.9%; Cardio-metabolic and Pain Management outperformed IPM by 1.7x and 1.4x respectively.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 15% organic revenue growth plus about 1.5-2% inorganic growth, for about 17% total revenue growth and 20% PAT growth.
Management says it aims to maintain margins 'within a similar range' but will not commit to sustaining Q1 levels given cost volatility.

Raw material: about 70-90 days of stock held at quarter end; new stocks began arriving in June 2026. Management sees possible 100 bps margin hit in coming quarters and is offsetting via other cost cuts.
Hormonal facility asset turnover expected below 1x in FY27, rising to 2-3x over about three years; depreciation on the INR130 crore capex is about INR6.5 crore a year.
Export ramp: dossiers ready by Nov-Dec 2026, then 12-18 months for registration; international launch targeted FY28-29.
Medical representative additions guided at 6-8% per year (about 200-250 MRs), with no MR additions planned in FY27 after about 400 were added in Q4 FY26.
capex_capacity: Europe-GMP hormonal (women's healthcare) facility commercialised on 30 June 2026, after INR130 crore capex; it handles tablets, soft gelatin capsules, ointments and gels.
Ahmedabad oral solid dosage facility Europe-GMP certification renewed.
Manufacturing mix is about 60% in-house and 40% outsourced, expected to stay similar through FY27.
API sourcing: about 60-65% of API needs are met by La Chandra Pharma Lab, in which the company holds a 31% stake (via Remedies Private Limited). La Chandra has EU GMP and a recent US DMF approval.
Hormonal plant to serve the domestic market initially; international dossier filings are in preparation.
demand_pricing: MAT June 2026 PharmaTrac split: volume growth 6.3% vs IPM 1.3%; price-led growth about 8.7% vs IPM 5.6%; new product contribution 3.4% vs IPM 2.9%.
Management says the Q1 India growth split is broadly in line with the MAT split.
Company ranks 26th in IPM (up from 29th a year ago). It is 5th in Women's Healthcare and Pain Management, 9th in Urology, and 20th in Cardio-diabeto (top 10 in new consolidated business).
Two brands now exceed INR100 crore annual revenue (one in MAT June 2023), and more than 40 brands exceed INR10 crore (from 32). Two new INR10 crore entrants are both organic.
Management expects IPM growth of about 9-11%, sustained since December 2025.
Semaglutide: management expects a INR1,500-1,800 crore market and targets a top-10 position, but says focus remains on engine brands.

qa_highlights.question: Is there scope for margin expansion if 20% growth continues, or will incremental growth be reinvested?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited favourable mix and operating leverage in Q1 but would not extrapolate. It said it aims to keep margins in a similar range and cited Southeast Asia and geopolitical cost risk.

qa_highlights.question: Did raw material inflation affect Q1, and will Q2 see more of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was largely unaffected due to 70-90 days of inventory. Management sees a possible 100 bps hit and is trying to offset it with other cost reductions to keep the 20% PAT guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the acquired Bayer-Zydus molecule (Dr. Reddy's-sourced, per the analyst) seem to decline YoY, and what is the path to 25% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: External revenue was INR28-30 crore, plus INR20 crore internal. Management called Q1 the launch quarter and said supply-chain integration took priority; it is targeting INR20-40 crore over the coming years.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 growth by volume, price and new launches, and IVF traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Split is in line with MAT: volume 6.3%, price 8.7%, new launches 3.4%. The IVF task force started in April 2026; management says it is too early to comment and will update in two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the employee and other expense ratios vs peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is high because about 1,000 MRs (35% of the 3,111 total) were added in three years and productivity per MR is lower; operating leverage should bring it down. Other expenses are mainly UCPMP-governed promotion costs, which are variable.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation and amortisation impact from the Wokadine and Bayer acquisitions, and from the hormonal plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Wokadine (INR97 crore plus GST) and Bayer (INR7 crore) are amortised over 10 years. The hormonal plant is depreciated over 20 years (about INR6.5 crore a year).

risks_watch: Raw material and geopolitical (Southeast Asia) cost pressure could cut gross margin by about 100 bps in coming quarters.
Hormonal facility under-recoveries until asset turnover rises from below 1x in FY27 toward 2-3x.
International revenue was flat in Q1; export ramp depends on dossier approvals (FY28-29).
Wokadine and Bayer-Zydus brand ramp is early; management guides to 25% inorganic growth over 2-3 years.
Dependence on La Chandra for about 60-65% of API needs.

544645|2026-03.headline: Park Medi World FY26 revenue rose 21% to INR1,679 crore and PAT 27% to INR274 crore, with gross debt cut to INR28 crore.
544645|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: revenue INR1,679 crore (+21% YoY), EBITDA INR444 crore (+20%, 26% margin) and PAT INR274 crore (+27%, 16% margin). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR460 crore (+30%), with operating EBITDA of INR127 crore (+44%, 28% margin) and PAT of INR77 crore (+47%). The bed network grew 610 beds to 3,610 at March 2026 (3,960 including Panchkula, commissioned 10 April 2026), and management reiterated a target of 5,460 beds by March 2028. Gross debt fell to INR28 crore from INR450 crore, and debtor days fell to 129 from 161.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating EBITDA excl. other income (Q4 FY26)

financial_highlights.change: +7% YoY for FY; Q4 vs INR28,423 in Q4 FY25

segments.name: IPD
segments.commentary: FY26 IPD volume was 95,525 (+18% YoY, highest ever); Q4 FY26 IPD was 25,329 (+29% YoY per the call).

segments.name: OPD
segments.commentary: FY26 OPD volume was about 7.78 lakh (+22% YoY); Q4 FY26 was about 1.88 lakh (+13% YoY). Total patients served about 8.7 lakh in FY26.

segments.name: High-end specialties
segments.commentary: About 56.9% of revenue came from high-end specialties in FY26, up 316 bps YoY. Oncology was about 6.5% of FY26 revenue versus 5% in FY25, and about 8% in Q4 FY26 versus 6% in Q4 FY25.

guidance_outlook: Bed capacity: 850 beds to be added in FY27 (350 Panchkula already commissioned, 200 Narela targeted for Q2 FY27, 300 Kanpur) and about 1,000 in FY28 (400 Gorakhpur, 200 Ambala oncology extension, 150 Mohali, 250 Rohtak Greenfield, which management said comes January 2028). Target 5,460 beds by March 2028 and, between FY28 and FY33, nearly 10,000 beds.

Capex: about INR55 crore planned in FY27 and about INR250 crore in FY28; management cited about INR500 crore total over the next two years. Capex per bed is about INR34 lakh through the 5,460-bed plan.

CGHS rate hike of about 12-15% is expected to add about 7-7.5% to revenue for nine months of FY27. Management's net impact estimate is 5-6% of total revenue. Actual flow-through likely visible after Q1 FY27.
Payor mix is expected to move from about 80:20 (government insurance vs cash/TPA) toward 75:25 and then 70:30 over 12-18 months. Management's end-FY26 target was about 65-70% government insurance.

Agra (commissioned February 2026) is adding about INR5 crore revenue per month, expected to contribute about INR90 crore revenue in FY27 and turn EBITDA positive. Bathinda (250 beds) is running at 65-70% occupancy.
Debtor days are expected to fall below 100 eventually, but management said this will take time; near-term target around four months of government collection cycle.

Two FY26 additions: Bathinda 250 beds (acquired, Punjab) and Agra 360 beds (UP entry, commissioned February 2026). Narela, Delhi (200 beds, IBC acquisition): total capex about INR80 crore, of which INR55 crore spent. Kanpur (300 beds): about INR30 crore to invest.

Greenfield break-even takes 12-15 months and full recovery 2.5-3 years, per management. Acquired assets' EBITDA break-even is about 3-3.5 years on a weighted average basis; acquisition investment recovered through revenue in roughly 11 months.
Liquidity: FDs of about INR314 crore, about INR100 crore in bank, and INR135 crore non-current FDs at 31 March 2026. Management expects only a small debt raise if any.
demand_pricing: Management says ARPOB is kept in the affordable range and is one of several profitability drivers; expenses should be benchmarked to revenue, not ARPOB alone.
Demand described as strong across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, with patients who previously travelled to metros now treated locally.

Collections are described as close to 100% by management. Government (central) accounts for 92% of debtors; government bills are cleared in about three months, and management is seeking to shorten this.
Disallowance on government revenue stayed at about 9% in Q4 FY26.
Oncology is being expanded across all 16 hospitals (medical and surgical), with radiation oncology in three hospitals.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin expansion, seasonality, CGHS or case mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said mainly higher occupancy at existing hospitals; Agra began operations in February 2026 and Bathinda in May (per CFO), so new units did not drive Q4 margins.

qa_highlights.question: Provision for receivables at FY26 end?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the provision made at 31 March 2026 is close to INR200 crore under Ind AS.

qa_highlights.question: Cost and break-even profile of Greenfield and acquired hospitals?

544657|2026-03.headline: FY26 total income rose 37.19% to INR256.92 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed to about 11% in H2 on forex and RCN prices; management guides 15-16%.

H2 saw margin compression from a spike in raw cashew nut (RCN) prices, forex movement (rupee moved about 10.5% from April 2025 base) and shipping disruptions, with H2 total income up 37.38% to INR138.5 crore and H2 PAT up 8.97%. Capacity utilisation was 86% on an 18,000 MT Andhra Pradesh plant, and a greenfield 35,000 MT Vizianagaram facility (targeting 70,000 MT total by FY30) is being built with INR39.53 crore of POs committed by March 2026.

qa_highlights.answer: FY25 plant was shut for expansion and stock was sold off. FY26 focused on institutional customers, which carry more credit. Inventory about INR38 crore and debtors about INR18 crore; creditors rose to about INR20 crore from INR3 crore.

544664|2026-03.headline: KSH International Q4 FY26 revenue rose 101% YoY to INR 1,018 crore and EBITDA per ton reached about INR 74,000, with FY26 PAT at a record INR 110 crore.
544664|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter: revenue from operations of INR 1,018 crore (up 101% YoY), EBITDA of INR 56 crore (from INR 35 crore), and a record quarterly PAT of INR 34.5 crore (up 87%). Volumes were about 7,600 metric tons, up 29% YoY, though Middle East shipments of roughly 100-150 tons slipped from March into April. Management said FY26 EBITDA per ton was about INR 67,600 and guided sustainable EBITDA per ton to a 65,000-74,000 range, with the Supa Phase II expansion (to about 59,000 MT) on track for FY27. Working capital days remain high at 65-68, and management is negotiating bank terms to push payable days above 25-30.

segments.commentary: Grew 58% in FY26 and 80% in Q4 YoY. Management is targeting EVs, AC compressors and motors. About 35% of the 43,445 MT installed capacity is standard.

Middle East impact was limited: some Gulf shipments were delayed by a few weeks and rerouted. Management estimated 200-300 tons of volume effect in Q4 including orders not started.

India CTC demand estimated at 100,000-120,000 tons by 2030 versus about 40,000 tons in FY25 and 70,000-75,000 tons expected in FY27-28. Imports were about 1,000 tons a month earlier and are expected to decline.
New entrants could take 5-7 years to qualify for 765 kV/HVDC CTC, according to management.
Pricing is set via one-year or multi-year value-addition matrices agreed with OEMs, not linked to copper price.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify the Middle East impact on Q4.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 100-150 tons of dispatches slipped from March to April. Later, the estimated total effect including orders not started was 200-300 tons.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA per ton for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 65,000-70,000 per ton is sustainable long term, and later gave 67,000-74,000 as the range.

qa_highlights.answer: Payable days are targeted above 25 days, and inventory days rose because large transformer orders need full manufacture before dispatch.

qa_highlights.answer: Specialized EBITDA per ton is about 3x standard. The blended mix is expected to continue, with both segments growing.

qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 30% of revenue, down from a high near 40%, and the target is to return to about 40% over the next couple of years. All exports go to T&D transformer OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for capacity beyond 59,000 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: Space exists for another 10,000 MT at Supa, with no decision yet. Management would not rule out adding capacity over 24 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any sign of demand deferment from domestic OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The customer base is diversified and management said it can redirect volumes to other customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will transformer makers backward integrate into CTC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see a general trend toward backward integration, given available capacity and the process complexity.

544679|2026-03.headline: Amagi FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,506 crores and turned PAT positive at INR 72 crores, swinging about INR 140 crores from a FY25 loss.
544679|2026-03.overview: Amagi reported its first full year as a listed company, with FY26 revenue of INR 1,506 crores (up 30% reported, 23% constant currency) and Q4 revenue of INR 397 crores (up 29%). Adjusted EBITDA rose to about INR 156 crores (10% margin) from INR 23 crores, and PAT was INR 72 crores versus a loss of INR 69 crores in FY25. Management stressed net revenue retention of 126% and growth across all three segments, while flagging Q4 gross margin compression tied to customer pricing, AI costs and parallel-running of lower-cost alternatives. NEWSPULSE, the first agentic AI product, has its first paying customer and is in trials with news networks.

Focus areas for FY27 are durable revenue growth, operating leverage and cash conversion.

544679|2026-06.headline: Amagi's July 7, 2026 "AI in Media" webinar was industry-level only; no quarterly financials, guidance or Amagi-specific metrics were disclosed.
544679|2026-06.overview: This transcript is of an educational investor webinar titled "AI in Media", hosted by Amagi on July 7, 2026 and filed under Regulation 30, not an earnings call. The moderator stated upfront that company financial performance, outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed. The CEO Baskar Subramanian framed AI as reshaping the video value chain across production, preparation (metadata, encoding, scheduling), distribution (agent-to-agent deals) and consumer discovery. He cited a claim that every $1 spent on technology brings $2 to $4 of human toil, and said most customers view AI as expansionary rather than a cost-saving tool today. No Q1 FY27 results, segment data or guidance were given.
guidance_outlook: No company guidance given; the moderator stated financial performance, business outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed.
Management described AI-driven production cost deflation as a multi-year shift, saying the next few years would bring a fundamental change, without quantifying it.
Management said outcome-based pricing is early and not yet visible in media, and that the core system is expected to stay as is while expansion revenue is driven by outcomes.
capex_capacity: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPUs and servers, and expects more progression in that direction; no Amagi capex or capacity figures were given.
Management said GPU costs are significant for video AI but did not quantify them; token cost is a small part of AI cost in video.
demand_pricing: Management says most customers are pursuing expansion (more channels, revenue opportunities) rather than AI cost savings today, citing Jevons' paradox.
Outcome-based pricing (per transaction, per result, per success) is being discussed in some markets, but management says it is not yet visible in media.

Management says token cost is a small part of AI cost in video; GPU costs are significant. It also cited an example of a scheduler's work falling from 8 hours to about 10 minutes of review under an agentic system.
Management described the metadata and preparation workload as a headcount constraint, with media companies creating about 6 hours of unique news daily and running content across 40-plus countries.

qa_highlights.question: What safeguards exist against hallucination and unpredictability given strict 99.9999% SLAs with clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the approach is to bring determinism to a non-deterministic problem through guardrails and engineered systems, noting that getting AI from demos to production is the hard part.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI improving prep-work speed and reducing pricing through deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI mainly reduces human cost in preparation (e.g., speech-to-text making subtitling unnecessary) and expands what can be done rather than directly reducing price.

qa_highlights.question: Can AI move production and pre-production workflows to the cloud?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPU and server capacity, and expects more of this shift.

qa_highlights.question: Are there real-life examples of cost reduction or higher OTT/cable content from AI?

544681|2026-03.headline: INDO SMC guided FY27 revenue to INR450-500 crores on an INR237 crore order book plus INR125 crore fresh orders, with margins targeted at 15%+.
544681|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first full year after listing, with management saying revenue roughly doubled and PAT more than doubled, driven by higher-value CT/PT, bus duct, meter cubicle and panel products. Management attributed a softer March-quarter SMC and FRP output to geopolitics-driven resin and petroleum-product price swings and supply gaps. The company shifted to shorter (2-3 month) orders with price-escalation clauses (5% trigger) and said it is now choosing orders on margin. Inventory rose to about INR85 crores (around 100 days) because of pre-stocked raw materials, and the working capital cycle was cut from 83 to about 40 days. Management did not give a precise FY26 revenue or margin figure in the call; the 15% EBITDA margin cited by analysts was not confirmed by management.

EBITDA margin (as cited by analyst, not confirmed by management)

segments.commentary: About INR120-125 crores of the order book; management said CT/PT is more engineering-intensive with margins above SMC/FRP, targeting above 18% EBITDA on standardised products. Currently operating at 11 kV and 33 kV, with 66 kV and above still in planning.

segments.name: Bus ducts, meter cubicles and panels
segments.commentary: Meter cubicle orders of INR10-15 crores were added, with new meter cubicle orders of INR10 crores-plus taken in the current period. Management described these as higher-margin lines bundled with SMC and CT/PT.

segments.name: SMC
segments.commentary: About INR80 crores of order book being executed month to month. Management said FY26 SMC and FRP output fell in March due to resin and petroleum-product shortages; the call did not give segment revenue figures.

segments.commentary: Remainder of the order book, executed against monthly clearances. Plan to add about 300 tons of FRP production capacity.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Early-stage: Oman and Gulf orders, samples sent to US and Germany, Dubai electrical fair planned from September. Management said UL 94 certification is a requirement for the US and that certification takes 1-2 months.

Railway clearance expected by end of the following month after the call, pending lab expansion; management said trial orders would grow over the next three years.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR25 crores (as disclosed in the IPO) is the first priority, covering machines and facilities across SMC, FRP and electrical engineering.
A 2,000-ton-plus SMC press is expected in 2-3 months, to enable larger railway products and big boxes; SMC capacity target is 6,000 tons-plus.
Nashik (Maharashtra) plant needs capex and more space; a second plant at Nashik has started production readiness. Ahmedabad is running well on utilisation.

Plans for 33 kV CTs and meter cubicles; a lab expansion funded from the IPO is expected to be completed by the end of the month after the call.
demand_pricing: Management said the utilities and electrical industry (SMC, FRP, CT/PT, LTCT, bus ducts, switchgear) is growing fast; it cited about 20 states served and a push to expand pan-India and export.

Competition in higher-kV CT/PT is limited: management said few players hold approvals, and cited ABB Crompton as operating at 66, 120 and 240 kV.

Raw materials: resin (SMC/FRP) and petroleum-linked inputs were the main pressure; glass fiber held in about 3 months' stock; copper and steel costs passed through at order time. Management said it took a hit on resin in March.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said SMC and FRP fell from March due to geopolitics-driven resin and petroleum shortages and rate swings. Order book: about INR125 crores in CT/PT and LTCT, about INR80 crores in SMC, and the rest in FRP and tarpaulin.

544684|2026-03.headline: Digilogic FY26 revenue rose 8.4% to INR78.27 crore and PAT 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, but a ~INR22 crore spillover from delayed imported hardware missed the 20-25% growth guidance.
544684|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income rose 8.4% YoY to INR78.27 crore, with EBITDA up 16.5% to INR15.18 crore and margin expanding 152 bps to 19.6%. PAT grew 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, and operating cash flow turned positive at INR12.63 crore. Management attributed the shortfall versus its January 2026 growth guidance to delayed imported OEM hardware, which pushed about INR22 crore of orders into FY27. Management guided to 20-25% growth for FY27, contingent on converting INR100-plus crore of orders by September 2026, and announced new subsidiary Abhedhya (RF systems), an SBC R&D effort, and Project UDAN manufacturing expansion.

segments.name: Measurement equipment
segments.commentary: About 49% of FY26 revenue; management said most of its value comes from software content with little material cost, supporting the margin gain.

segments.name: Checkout systems
segments.commentary: About 22% of FY26 revenue; ATEs about 17%. Management said ATE and checkout value was broadly flat YoY, and the share fell because measurement equipment grew.

segments.name: Prototyping vs production
segments.commentary: Management estimated roughly 30% of revenue from prototyping and 70% from production orders. This was not reconciled with a reported figure and was described as approximate.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25%, reiterated on the call; management said it is confident of meeting it.
Management targets INR100-plus crore of purchase orders by end-September 2026, with billing for FY27 expected to be supported by that order intake.
Order book was about INR30-plus crore as of 30 May 2026, with most expected to bill by August 2026.

Project UDAN (new manufacturing facility, about four times the current capacity) expected operational by mid-2028; indicative revenue INR11-13 crore in FY29, INR28-30 crore in FY30, INR57-61 crore in FY31.
Current setup capacity estimated at INR150-160 crore revenue potential.
Abhedhya (RF subsidiary) expected to demonstrate systems in 8-12 months; management indicated revenue in FY28, not FY27.
capex_capacity: Project UDAN: a manufacturing and environmental testing facility, about four times current size; mid-2028 target; can deliver 20-25 systems per six months versus about six currently.
Guest house under construction; capitalised finance cost on exposure of about INR2.1 crore (not fully drawn), borrowing at REPO plus 2.5%.
Abhedhya, a new RF subsidiary for radar, EW and communication subsystems, with a 1-year build-and-demonstrate timeline.
R&D: custom single board computer (SBC) built in-house by an eight-member team, about 1.5-2 years old; qualification range -20 to +85 degrees C; environmental testing not yet completed.
Management said two to three new R&D products are in development.
demand_pricing: FY26 execution was held back by imported hardware from US/European OEMs; lead time rose from about 2 months to about 4 months, leaving roughly INR22 crore spilled into April 2026. Management said about INR20 crore additional revenue would otherwise have closed in FY26.

Order book fell to about INR31 crore from INR46 crore; the tender pipeline fell to about INR110 crore from INR200 crore. Management attributed this to Government fund reallocation and said projects are delayed 6-8 months rather than lost.
Management said OEMs are rerouting shipments, adding a week or 10 days and roughly 1-2% cost.
Competitors named: Data Patterns and Zen Technologies, mainly in prototyping. Management said production work under DCPP is nomination-based with limited competition.
Customer base is 100% government in substance (DRDO, BDL, BEL, public sector defence production agencies), with some transactions billed through BDL.
Management said the export route is via DRDO and BDL systems, and MoUs with Sperry and Eirad are at the evaluation stage toward Tier-1 aerospace supply chains.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 guidance of 20-25% growth missed, and what supports FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported hardware arrived about 4 months after order rather than 2, leaving roughly INR22 crore of spillover. Management cited INR30-plus crore of orders in hand by 30 May and a target of INR100-plus crore of POs by September.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall from INR46 crore to INR31 crore and the pipeline from INR200 crore to INR110 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government fund reallocation changed priorities and projects are delayed 6-8 months rather than cancelled. The INR100-plus crore target covers only projects with budgets allocated or tenders out.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue comes from production versus prototyping?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said roughly 30% prototyping and 70% production, and deferred exact figures to the CFO. No reported split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why set up Abhedhya as a separate company rather than a division?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RF work needs different people, salaries, infrastructure and design expertise than TMS, and separate accountability is needed. Tender qualification is to be built by demonstrating products first.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ATE and checkout share fall from about 44% to 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said measurement equipment, mostly software value add with low material cost, grew to a similar scale, and ATE and checkout value was broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the order book converting to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Current orders should bill by about August 2026. Pipeline orders are expected as POs by end-September, with 2-3 months of build and about one month of installation, and cash collection around Aug-Oct.

Governance: management's FY26 growth guidance was missed, and the call shows the company's first results call as a newly listed SME.

rows.why: MoUs with Sperry and Eirad are at evaluation stage toward Tier-1 aerospace supply chains, with no revenue figure given.

544684|2026-09.headline: Digilogic H1 FY27 revenue rose 91% to INR34.96 crores and PAT rose 151% to INR4.76 crores, with management reiterating 25-30% FY27 top-line growth.

544685|2026-03.headline: Shadowfax Q4 FY26 revenue about INR 1,237 crores (+74% YoY) with record 4.5% PAT margin; FY26 PAT INR 112 crores.
544685|2026-03.overview: Management reported record Q4 FY26 growth and profitability: revenue about INR 1,237 crores (+74% YoY, +6.7% QoQ), adjusted EBITDA about INR 58 crores (4.7% margin vs 4.3% in Q3 and 0.7% a year ago) and PAT INR 56 crores (4.5% margin). For FY26, revenue exceeded INR 4,200 crores (+69%), adjusted EBITDA was about INR 159 crores (roughly 3x FY25) and PAT was INR 112 crores vs INR 6 crores. Management guided to 27-30% overall growth, 100-120 bps adjusted EBITDA margin improvement through FY28, and FY27 capex of INR 180-190 crores, while investing in real estate, dark stores and large-shipment coverage.

segments.name: Express parcel

segments.name: Hyperlocal
segments.commentary: Grew more than 50% YoY and 16% QoQ in Q4; quick commerce volumes picked up and operations with Amazon Now commenced. Management guides 45-50% growth for this segment in the next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY26 margin expansion look better as capex normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said significant operating leverage is yet to come, with opex from investments returning in FY27-FY28, and that H2 capex was made in advance for FY27 capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Dark store unit economics and ROIC?

qa_highlights.question: Margin guidance basis and service EBITDA?

qa_highlights.question: Lost shipment cost and white goods impact?
qa_highlights.answer: About half of the roughly 6% is quality-check debits from reverse logistics and half pure losses; management cited image-recognition upgrades and fixes in large-parcel damages in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Amazon Shipping and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said captive arms deprioritise external customers at peak, so they do not see such models working in India; D2C/SME is a meaningful double-digit share of revenue, not disclosed exactly.

Hyperlocal YoY growth slowed in Q4 due to a strong prior-year Q4 base; competition in quick commerce crowdsourcing from platforms like LoadShare.

544685|2026-06.headline: Shadowfax Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR1,358 crore; management raised FY27 growth guidance to 38-40% from 27-30%.
544685|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 65% YoY to INR1,358 crore and 10% QoQ, the fifth straight quarter of 65%+ growth. Adjusted EBITDA rose to INR67 crore (4.9% margin vs 4.7% in Q4) and PAT hit a record INR65 crore. Management attributed margin gains to lower lost-shipment costs (5.5% of revenue vs 6.1% in Q4) and efficiency work that absorbed diesel and labour cost pressure. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 38-40% while keeping the margin trajectory unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 capex is for the growth upgrade versus beyond FY27?

544685|2026-09.headline: Shadowfax Q2 FY27 revenue rose 57% YoY to INR1,538 crore with adjusted EBITDA margin of 5%, its first time crossing INR1,500 crore and 5%.
544685|2026-09.overview: Revenue reached INR1,538 crore, up 57% YoY and 13% QoQ, despite no festive sales-season revenue in the quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was INR77 crore at a 5% margin and PAT was INR67 crore. Operating space expanded from 53 lakh to 69 lakh sq ft ahead of the festive peak, and the delivery partner base grew 31% QoQ. Management kept the 27%-30% long-term growth guidance but declined to revise near-term guidance until Q3 performance is seen. Management also announced a micro-fulfillment centre (MFC) business and disclosed that exposure to the largest customer fell by at least 3-4 percentage points versus its long-term average.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,096 crore (+55% YoY, +10% QoQ) on 21.7 crore shipments; share of revenue fell to 71% from 73% in Q1. Express realization was broadly flat QoQ and marginally down YoY.

segments.name: Hyperlocal
segments.commentary: Revenue INR341 crore (+88% YoY, +26% QoQ); share of revenue rose to 22% from 20%. Realization per order rose about 13% QoQ, helped by longer-distance food delivery after aggregators moved to 0% commission.

segments.name: Other logistics services (CriticaLog, Dark Stores, value-added)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR100 crore, up 13% QoQ, as CriticaLog (serving more than 550 customers) and Dark Stores scale. Value-added services are guided at 35%-40% of revenue.

segments.name: Prime Large (bulky)
segments.commentary: Annualized run rate above INR100 crore, up 33% QoQ; white goods and value-added services are in pilot.

segments.name: D2C and SME (Shadowfax 360)
segments.commentary: D2C business more than doubled YoY, with market share above 14% (up 2 pp QoQ). Shadowfax 360 has more than 6,700 sellers ordering within 200 days of launch.

Management cited a 0% commission model in food delivery as a driver of higher-realization longer-distance orders.

qa_highlights.question: Given the festive season shift to Q3, will guidance be revised upward in the near and medium term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will wait for Q3 results before revising guidance; the 27%-30% long-term growth guidance is maintained, and it is too early to judge the rest of the sale season.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Hyperlocal realization increase, and how long will it last?
qa_highlights.answer: Realization rose from about INR55 to above INR60, driven by distance and mix: higher on-demand and long-distance orders, plus food delivery growth after the 0% commission model.

qa_highlights.question: What cost build-up hit margins ahead of the season?
qa_highlights.answer: Rental cost rose from 3.2% to 3.5% of revenue (about 30 bps), and depreciation rose slightly. Last-mile and contractual labour scaling had no P&L impact because of the crowdsourced model.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lower dependence on the main customer seasonal or strategic?
qa_highlights.answer: Exposure fell by at least 3-4 pp from the long-term average this quarter. Management attributes it to strategy (growth in D2C, SME, Prime Large and Hyperlocal), with the enterprise business growing more slowly.

qa_highlights.question: How do MFCs differ from Dark Stores, and is the capex inside the 3.8%-4% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Dark Stores deliver in 15-30 minutes; MFCs target 8-12 hour delivery from 40,000-50,000 sq ft sites with 5-10 co-located brands near city-edge sort centres. The capex guidance includes MFCs and Dark Stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Express realizations flat despite more Prime Large and D2C mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix effects (weight, zones, and shorter-distance Prime orders) offset gains. Realization was marginally up QoQ, marginally down YoY, and is expected to stay in a similar range short term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value-added services mix and the 2-year outlook for Express versus Hyperlocal?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added services are 35%-40% of revenue and are expected to hold that ratio over 3-5 years. Express and Hyperlocal are not expected to shift materially in mix over the next two years.

544695|2026-03.headline: Msafe FY26 revenue rose about 45% to Rs 103.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 39.49% and PAT at Rs 22.02 crore (+72%).
544695|2026-03.overview: Management's first earnings call after IPO reported FY26 revenue from operations of about Rs 103.5 crore (up ~45% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 49.9 crore (up ~57%) and PAT of Rs 22.02 crore (up ~72%). EBITDA margin widened to 39.49% from 36.55%, driven by the rental mix and utilisation. Management said MS scaffolding capacity has reached about 6,285 tonnes via temporary rented-premise facilities, ahead of IPO timelines, and entered aluminium formwork. Guidance calls for ~50% CAGR, with the mix shifting toward lower-margin sales, rising capex (~Rs 130 crore) and rising debt.

segments.name: Aluminium scaffolding
segments.commentary: ~Rs 98 crore in FY26, roughly split 50-50 sales and rental; current run-rate cited as ~Rs 3 crore/month sales and ~Rs 3.5 crore/month rental. Rental yield 60-66% p.a.; sales gross margin ~30%. Targeted growth ~20% in FY27 core business.

segments.commentary: Flagship product launched in FY26; machinery ordered, production targeted by end-June 2026. First-year target Rs 30-40 crore; gross margin guided at ~10% initially, ~15% long term. Management expects at least 30% of revenue from rental.

segments.commentary: Ladder manufacturing started, with a proposed channel partner model (none currently). Trading of industrial safety products deferred 3-4 months; no manufacturing planned for those.

guidance_outlook: Management says it expects ~50% CAGR, and later cited a 50-70% CAGR aim; it confirmed FY27 revenue of 'definitely' above Rs 150 crore is achievable but declined to commit to a PAT figure.

FY27 revenue mix expected around 40% rental and 60% sales; sales share may rise to 60-40 or 38-72 range.

capex_capacity: MS scaffolding capacity doubled to ~6,285 tonnes (cited as 62.85 lakh units) via temporary facilities on rented premises; running near full utilisation, sometimes 24 hours.

IPO proceeds: ~25% used for rental assets by FY26 (rest by 2H FY27); ~11% used for manufacturing and rental expansion, with land acquisition advanced and advanced machines ordered.
demand_pricing: Operating at ~1,000-1,500 sites with ~2,500 customers; pan-India presence versus mostly regional peers; ~20 years of operating experience.
Sales are short-cycle (orders up to 7 days), so aluminium price changes are passed on; rental rates are sticky, so the company absorbs some cost increases.
Aluminium prices reportedly up 40-50%; the company holds large inventory, with a 30% year-end price increase cited, so benefit is not yet fully on the books.
Bad debts under 2% over six years; new customers pay 1-3 months' rental as advance.
Competition: management says there are no entry barriers, with Technocraft cited as a possible entrant in rental and formwork.

qa_highlights.question: Is steel capacity at peak utilisation, and what is the revenue from it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the factory is fully occupied, running around the clock. Steel generates ~Rs 1 crore/month rental and ~Rs 1 crore/month sales, with ~70% of material on rent and 25-30% sold.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ~40% EBITDA and ~22% PAT margins sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the mix to change as formwork (mostly sales) and steel grow. The 40% margin may fluctuate slightly, but the company aims to hold the range.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins and EBITDA evolve with lower-margin segments growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the EBITDA percentage may decline but absolute impact is minimal, and topline growth will offset this. It said its internal targets are much higher than guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How will capex and debt be funded in FY27?

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited project-based needs, multi-site logistics, capital constraints, and scaffolding being under 1% of project cost. Yields reflect short economic life (aluminium ~5 years vs steel 10-15), with scrap value recoverable.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory up to ~Rs 24 crore and ~80 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose from yard expansion (4 to 18), a 30% year-end metal price rise, and precautionary stock; management expects normalisation over time.

Competitive entry in rental (e.g., Technocraft) could compress the 32-66% yields that drive profitability.
Aluminium and steel price volatility, rental rate stickiness and inventory valuation; ~Rs 2.87 crore loss on scrapped or lost assets, which management says is recurring.
Factory-level attrition above 50%, per the call.

544695|2026-06.headline: Msafe Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 40% YoY to ₹31.79 crore and PAT rose 44% to ₹7.27 crore, with the rental business up 24%.

Capacity remains the binding constraint: the Kosi Kotwan (Mathura) integrated plant targets operations by May 2027, and the formwork line is now targeted for December 2026 after machine delivery delays.

544695|2026-09.headline: Msafe Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 53% YoY to Rs 40 crore and PAT rose 55% to Rs 8.49 crore, with management reiterating 50-70% top-line and 40-50% bottom-line growth guidance.
544695|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations up 53% YoY to about Rs 40 crore, EBITDA up 49% to Rs 15.61 crore at a 38.65% margin, and PAT up 55% to Rs 8.49 crore. H1 FY27 revenue rose 47% to Rs 72 crore and PAT rose 50% to Rs 15.76 crore. Rental contributed 51.5% of Q2 revenue, and the warehouse network expanded from 21 to 24 locations. MS scaffolding capacity was raised from about 3,200 tonnes per annum pre-IPO to a 9,000 tonnes target, now revised to 15,000 tonnes, and formwork commercial sales are expected to start within about a month.

financial_highlights.change: down from 39.67% in the prior-year period as stated on the call

segments.name: Scaffolding rental (MS and aluminium)
segments.commentary: Rental was 51.5% of Q2 revenue; management said it expects rental at about 52% and sales at 48% for H1, with rental the core focus. Rental yields are 32-38% for MS scaffolding and 60-66% for aluminium scaffolding.

segments.name: Scaffolding sales
segments.commentary: Sales contributed about 48-49% of revenue. Sales mix rose in Q2, which management said diluted EBITDA margin by about one percentage point.

segments.name: Formwork (new, aluminium-based)
segments.commentary: Initial capacity of 500 tonnes per annum at a rented facility, with trial runs started and commercialisation targeted for December 2026. Management expects it to contribute at least 15% of total business over time, but not a significant amount in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of 50-70% annually and PAT growth of 40-50% annually, reiterated; management said it has met or exceeded past commitments and sees no threat to guidance.
FY27 revenue growth target of 50%, driven by capacity additions, warehouse expansion, improved leverage and gradual commercialisation of formwork.
PAT margin expected to stay above 20% in FY27 with about one percentage point variation; formwork may contribute 15-20% of total revenue with similar margins if achieved.
Management aims for both top-line and bottom-line growth at similar rates in FY28 and beyond, but gave no specific PAT margin range.
Management wants to be cash-flow positive for the full year FY27 but said becoming debt-free in the near term may be difficult.

Integrated manufacturing facility at Mathura under construction, expected to become operational in May 2027.
Capex and working capital requirement of Rs 20-25 crore for completing the factory and meeting working capital; total debt expected to rise to about Rs 65-70 crore from about Rs 44 crore.
Lightweight aluminium-based formwork plant: 500 tonnes per annum at a rented facility, trial runs started, commercialisation targeted for December 2026.
Warehouse network expanded from 21 to 24 locations.
demand_pricing: Management said demand for both scaffolding and MS scaffolding is very strong; scaffolding utilisation is nearly 80%, and MS utilisation is high enough that the company had to repeatedly revise capacity targets.
Average scaffolding rental order is about four months; MS rental tenure averages about one year, with individual contracts from three months to two years.

Demand drivers cited: data centres (over 100 large data centres and about 10 semiconductor plants under construction), Navi Mumbai and Bhogapuram airports, malls, hotels and government and private infrastructure.
Management said 10-15 new players are entering the formwork market, but sees significant demand; differentiation is claimed from organised pan-India wholesale operations.

Exports at about 7-8% of total revenue expected this year, mainly to certain Middle Eastern countries; products are sold rather than rented overseas. Europe approvals are obtained (EN 1004 standard); Australia requires different approvals.
Management said it could not disclose specific export countries for commercial reasons.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of rental and sales for H1 FY27, and how will the mix evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix is broadly similar, varying by one to two percentage points. Previous period was 49% sales and 51% rental; the current period is 48% sales and 52% rental. Management aims to keep rental at least 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 50% growth guidance and is there oversupply risk from competitors such as Teamtech in formwork?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is driven by new capacity, the warehouse network, and formwork. Management said 10-15 new players are entering, but demand is significant. Formwork is concentrated in metros and is expanding to Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new formwork segment contribute meaningfully, and how big can it get?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a significant contributor in FY27 given long enquiry-to-execution cycles. Management expects it to contribute at least 15% of the total business over time.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAT margin stay above 20% and what PAT range is targeted for FY28 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: PAT margin may vary by one percentage point. Formwork may contribute 15-20% of total revenue with similar margins. Management aims for similar top-line and bottom-line growth in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak debt requirement for the capex, and can the company become debt-free?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex and working capital need is Rs 20-25 crore on top of about Rs 44 crore of existing debt, taking total debt to about Rs 65-70 crore. Management said becoming debt-free in the near term may be difficult, as the business is asset-intensive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economic life and payback of MS versus aluminium scaffolding, and how does yield compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Economic life is 15-20 years for MS and 5-7 years for aluminium. Rental yield is 32-38% for MS and 60-66% for aluminium. Scrap residual value is 50% or more. Management said lower MS yield is offset by longer life and a larger addressable market.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline from 39.67% to 38.65%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the change to product mix, with higher sales of lower-margin products carrying 5-6% margin. Depreciation uses the written-down method, so reported profit may rise over time. Management said the margin is still in line with guidance of 35%.

qa_highlights.question: How have trade receivables changed, and what are the receivable days?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days fell 15 days, from 90 to 75. Receivables rose to Rs 30 crore from Rs 23 crore last year, but the exact recovery amount was not available.

544698|2026-03.headline: H2 FY26 total income rose 28% YoY to INR12,656.59 lakh and net profit rose 158% to INR432.20 lakh; FY26 PAT was INR750.29 lakh.
544698|2026-03.overview: PAN HR Solution's first earnings call, held 12 June 2026 after its February 2026 BSE SME listing, covered H2 and full-year FY26 results. Management reported H2 total income of INR12,656.59 lakh (+28% YoY) and H2 net profit of INR432.20 lakh (+158% YoY), against a prior-year H2 that was smaller. Full-year PAT of INR750.29 lakh looked moderate because FY25 included a one-time INR6.5 crore prior-period income. The company ended FY26 with net worth of INR3,751 lakh, cash of INR2,434 lakh and no debt, and set out a plan to reach INR1,000 crore revenue by FY29.

financial_highlights.change: Full-year YoY comparison not stated; FY25 base included INR6.5 crore one-time exceptional prior-period income

segments.name: Manpower outsourcing / workforce deployment
segments.commentary: Deployed workforce grew from about 10,000 at IPO to over 11,000 on payroll as of the call. Clients are concentrated in e-commerce, quick commerce, logistics, warehousing and manufacturing; management cited more than 17 clients.

segments.name: Emerging services (3PL, payroll, compliance, HR outsourcing, white-collar hiring)
segments.commentary: Management said these are new or being scaled: 3PL and B2B models were not previously done, and white-collar one-time staffing has started. No revenue figures were given for these lines.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow FY27 turnover by approximately 40%.
Target revenue of INR1,000 crore by FY29 (within three years), with the 3PL model named as the first growth lever.
Priorities for FY27: deploy IPO proceeds into working capital, move toward pay-and-collect contracts, expand into new geographies and sectors, and grow payroll, compliance and HR services.
Management expects a higher-margin mix over time, but said some contracts carry lower margins while creating operating leverage.
capex_capacity: Workforce deployment rose from about 10,000 at IPO to more than 11,000 on payroll; the company said it now operates in the South and West as well as North and East.
Management said internal infrastructure is underused and that new services can run on existing infrastructure without major new investment.
IPO proceeds are to go mainly to working capital expansion, and acquisitions are under consideration; no specific acquisition target or deal size was named.
demand_pricing: Revenue in FY26 was affected by contract repricing and billing-cycle changes, as stated by management.

Management said it had turned away pay-and-collect clients in the prior year because of fund constraints and can now pursue them; pay-and-collect has started at one or two locations with existing clients.
Competitive positioning rests on compliance credibility (operating since 2015), balance-sheet strength, and an integrated single-window model covering salary, compliance and workforce management.
Management did not quantify pricing or margin changes.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors read moderate full-year growth versus strong H2 numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 shows strong growth; the full-year PAT gap reflects a FY25 base that included INR6.5 crore one-time prior-period income. It attributed the revenue slowdown to not taking pay-and-collect clients in FY25 for lack of funds.

qa_highlights.question: How will the IPO capital be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: First priority is business expansion and working capital; the company is also watching acquisition opportunities. No amount or timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the acquisition targets and why acquire?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets are workforce management, staffing and payroll companies with strong client bases; the rationale is to gain client databases and avoid duplicating infrastructure. No named targets or valuation were disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the INR1,000 crore FY29 revenue goal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the 3PL business with existing clients (not previously pursued due to funds), new areas, stronger existing-client relationships and acquisitions, targeting completion within three years.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins come under pressure with growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some contracts carry lower margins but generate operating leverage; the focus is on profitable growth and improving return ratios.

qa_highlights.question: What are the return-ratio expectations (ROE, ROCE)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said return ratios are a priority; temporary dips are possible while capital is deployed for growth. No ROE or ROCE figures were given.

risks_watch: Full-year PAT comparison is distorted by the FY25 one-time INR6.5 crore income; the underlying base needs confirming.
Revenue was hit by contract repricing and billing-cycle changes in FY26; watch whether these persist in FY27.

The 40% FY27 turnover target and INR1,000 crore FY29 goal depend on working-capital deployment, pay-and-collect contracts (which raise working-capital needs) and acquisitions with no named targets yet.
Margin dilution from lower-margin contracts and the new 3PL, white-collar and pay-and-collect mix.
Client concentration: management cited more than 17 clients, which is a small base for the stated scale-up.
The company said it has no debt, but no quarterly or segment breakdown was given.
544698|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and the balance sheet, but vague on specifics: acquisition targets, segment revenue, margins and return ratios were given only in general terms. Answers on the FY26 full-year profit gap were more defensive, and several answers repeated the strategy without numbers.
key_quotes: Our H2 revenue for FY 2025 increased from INR98.85 crores to INR126.57 crores this year, which shows a 28% year-on-year growth.
Investors should look at financial year 2026 as a stronger and clearer reflection of the company's actual business performance and earnings quality.

rows.why: IPO proceeds are partly earmarked for acquisitions and management is watching targets with strong client bases, but no named target, valuation or deal size was disclosed.

rows.why: Net worth was INR3,751 lakh with cash of INR2,434 lakh and no debt, which gives funding room for working capital and acquisitions without borrowing.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 growth, the balance sheet and the INR1,000 crore FY29 goal, but gave no numbers on acquisitions, segment revenue, margins or return ratios; questions on the FY26 full-year profit gap and the margin trade-off got more defensive answers.

544699|2026-03.headline: Aye Finance Q4 FY26 profit rose 100% QoQ to INR86 crore, with credit cost down to 4.3% and FY27 guidance of 25-30% AUM growth.
544699|2026-03.overview: Aye Finance closed FY26 with AUM of INR7,044 crore (up 27% YoY, 6% QoQ) and Q4 disbursements of INR1,655 crore (up 26% QoQ). Q4 profit was INR86 crore, up 110% YoY and 100% QoQ, with FY26 profit up 13% to INR194 crore. Asset quality improved for a fifth straight quarter, with credit cost at 4.3%, PAR X at 6.9% and GNPA at 4.77%. Management guided FY27 to 25-30% AUM growth, 3.5-4% credit cost, 8.25-8.75% opex ratio and 4-4.5% ROA, with borrowing costs expected to fall 25-35 bps.

segments.name: Mortgage loans
segments.commentary: Mortgage is 23% of portfolio vs 12% in FY24; PAR 90 at about 2.7% (up vs December quarter), PAR X at about 4.1%, with a target PAR 90 of 2-2.5%. Book is about INR1,500-1,600 crore per management, versus INR1,300-1,400 crore in an analyst's figure.

segments.name: Hypothecation loans
segments.commentary: Secured hypothecation is about 40-47% of book (figures differed in the call) and unsecured hypothecation about 37%. Unsecured HL is said to behave like the secured book; management sees yields stable.

segments.name: CGFMU-covered book
segments.commentary: Roughly INR500 crore of hypothecation book is covered under CGFMU as of March 2026; the company has not used CGTMSE.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guided at 25-30%; opex growth of about 15% is expected to support this.
FY27 credit cost guided at 3.5-4%, with Q4 FY27 expected at 3-3.25%; three-year asset quality target 3.25-3.75%.
Opex ratio to fall to 8.25-8.75% in FY27 from 9.6% in FY26; three-year opex guidance about 7-7.5% per analyst's reading.
ROA target of 4-4.5% with leverage of 4-4.5x (total assets to borrowings) and ROE in the high teens; management says this is reachable within FY27.

Borrowing cost expected to fall 25-35 bps from the FY26 level (management later clarified from the Q4 blended 10.87%), driven by replacing high-cost debt, a possible rating upgrade from A stable and partly offset by rising rates.
PAR X to fall to 5.5-6% over FY27 (about 100-150 bps), with about 30 bps in H1. Profit split expected at 35-40% in H1 and 60-65% in H2.
capex_capacity: Presence in 18 states and 3 union territories with 571 branches, 6.40 lakh+ active borrowers, and 70+ business clusters; branches are mainly Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns.
FY26 staffing rose 17-18%; mortgage manpower rose about 30% and collections team about 70%. FY27 manpower growth is expected to normalise to about 10%, mostly in branch sales and collections.
Collections capacity is to be redeployed to clean up NPA and write-off portfolio.
Management plans at least one new product launch in FY27 (gold loan, solar-based business lending or others), with market research due by end of Q1.
Mortgage share targeted at 30-35% of the portfolio over the next two to three years.
demand_pricing: Management says the micro-MSME segment is recovering, with rural consumption and formalisation supporting working-capital demand; April collections are not materially different from Q4 and April disbursements are seasonally lower.
Yield on hypothecation loans is stable; the blended yield falls as mortgage share rises, offset by lower cost of borrowing.
Management says it is not seeing a West Asia impact in March data, and the customer base is not linked to organised supply chains.
Collection efficiency: non-OD CE improved from 99.1% in Oct-25 to 99.5% in Mar-26; Bucket 1 CE rose from 51.8% to 62.5%. Stage 2 (30+60 DPD) is 1.12% of the portfolio.
Competition was not discussed in depth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the product mix changing, and what is the target secured/unsecured split?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage is 23% of book, target 30-35% in 2-3 years. Balance is hypothecation, with about 40% secured and about 30% unsecured. Management says 96% of customers own residential or commercial property.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NIM flat in FY27 guidance despite the equity raise and lower cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says mortgage mix lowers yield, offset by replacing old debt at 10.13% incremental cost, worth 30-35 bps. Q3 NIM was 14.2% and Q4 16.4%, mostly from lower borrowing costs and less borrowing after the IPO. NIM is guided to stay level.

qa_highlights.question: Why has credit cost fallen only gradually despite collection efficiency recovering?
qa_highlights.answer: The NPA pool still bulges from early crisis slippages; more than 70% is provided in the hypothecation NPA book. Credit cost should decline from Q2-Q3 FY27, reaching 3-3.25% by Q4 FY27. Stage 3 PCR is to stay above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in non-interest income in Q4 and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise came from fair value gains on mutual funds and a cross-currency swap impact. The net effect is about INR10-11 crore. The company plans to move these fair value items to OCI from April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What are the mortgage PAR 90 and sustainable GNPA levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage PAR 90 is about 2.7%, up from December, with PAR X at 4.1%. Target PAR 90 is 2-2.5% and credit cost below 2% on the mortgage book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the borrowing maturity profile?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2,400 crore of borrowings fall due in the next 12 months, at an average cost of about 10.95%, which management describes as relatively expensive debt.

risks_watch: Credit cost path depends on collection efficiency holding and on resolution of the NPA pool; FY27 credit cost guidance of 3.5-4% depends on this.
Rising market interest rates could offset the 25-35 bps borrowing-cost decline; management says priority-sector status limits the impact.
Mortgage PAR 90 rose QoQ to about 2.7%; the mortgage book is new and its credit cost is still elevated.
The opex ratio must fall from 9.6% to 8.25-8.75% while AUM grows 25-30%.
Possible rating review from A stable could lower borrowing costs, but timing is not specified.
Management did not give a timeline for a new product launch beyond end-Q1 market research.
544699|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and constructive on asset quality, profitability and FY27 targets, with the company citing the guidance as conservative. Less precise on some numbers, with corrections made on the cost of borrowing base and secured/unsecured splits.
key_quotes: Our expectation is that for the guidance would be that for FY26, we will target a growth in the range of 25% to 30%.
we expect to be guided in our workings on a 3.5% to 4% credit cost, supported by better portfolio quality and sustained collection efficiencies.
So we strongly believe that the opex can be brought down to the 8.25% to 8.75%
Our PAR X or PAR 1 plus, whatever you want to call it, stood at 6.9%, improving from 7.6% in quarter 3 of FY26.

rows.why: About INR2,400 crore of borrowings due in 12 months at ~10.95% average cost are being replaced, and the Q4 incremental cost of 10.13% is below the blended 10.87%, so a ~30 bps decline is guided.

rows.when: H1 FY27 for ~30 bps, full year by Q4 FY27
rows.why: PAR X fell from 7.6% in Q3 to 6.9% in Q4 (down 70 bps QoQ) and is guided to drop a further 100-150 bps, with about 30 bps in H1.
