rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: INR250 cr Chhapara capex (INR100 cr buildings, INR150 cr plant) lifts machine-hour capacity from 31-32 lakh to 42-43 lakh, staged as machines are installed; new facility starts commercial operations in FY28 and is running 1-1.5 months late.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 35-40% YoY revenue growth, backed by execution of two anchor orders at about INR50 cr run-rate ramping over years one to five, and about INR1,000 cr of short-cycle (6-18 months) orders within the INR3,000 cr+ book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The INR250 cr two-facility programme is already committed, so a fresh announcement is not needed; utilisation is about flat at 31-32 lakh hours, not clearly at 80%+ stress, and land in Ahmedabad and Hyderabad has no capex plan yet.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Order book above INR3,000 cr as of 31 July 2026 (incl. multi-year Weatherford order above USD100 mn) and Q1 revenue +61.5% YoY, but guidance is a 35-40% YoY range for FY28, with no near-term raise signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Capex running 1-1.5 months behind schedule because of rain, working capital still at 233 days, net debt/equity up to 0.41x from 0.34x, and defence/aerospace approvals (Nadcap, FA) may take 6-15 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Defence and aerospace first articles are underway with some revenue expected in FY27 and more in FY28, though Nadcap approval timing is uncertain (6-15 months); Others segment was 6.9% of Q1 revenue.

rows.label: Anchor orders ramp (INR2,000 cr over 3-5 years)
rows.why: About INR2,000 cr relates to two large orders with 3-5 year execution, execution has started with an expected run-rate of about INR50 cr and more, and about INR1,000 cr is short-cycle (6-18 months).

rows.label: Further working-capital release
rows.why: NWC days fell from 294 to 233 (target a further 10-20% improvement, reference below 200-220 days), but management said MOQ needs for new FAs may keep inventory high (inventory days 182 vs 225 at FY26-end).

rows.label: Raw-material pass-through lag
rows.why: Management claims 100% pass-through with a 2-3 month lag, but raw-material cost rose sequentially (cited 20%, 24%, then 28%), so near-term gross margin could compress before pass-through catches up.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, the INR3,000 cr+ order book and Chhapara capacity, but cautious and evasive on margin drivers, the raw-material lag, FA/defence approval timing and the rise in net debt to equity to 0.41x.

544726|2026-03.headline: Kotyark FY26 revenue Rs 314.9 crore, EBITDA Rs 48 crore, PAT Rs 19.4 crore, at only 7-8% capacity utilisation after Rajasthan expansion to 1,500 KLPD.
544726|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of Rs 314.9 crore, EBITDA of Rs 48 crore and PAT of Rs 19.4 crore while running at roughly 7-8% capacity utilisation. The Rajasthan biodiesel plant was expanded from 500 KLPD to 1,500 KLPD, taking cumulative annual capacity to about 4,80,000 KL. Management cited an executable order book of about Rs 80 crore and a pipeline of about Rs 215 crore, and announced two new 200 KLPD plants at Jhajjar and Kanpur due by December 2026. Management guided utilisation to rise towards 60-70% over several years, with near-term growth of 15-20% stated. Several answers were vague or inconsistent, and the call did not provide quarterly figures or a specific capex amount.

segments.name: Biodiesel (OMC and industrial)
segments.commentary: Rajasthan (Sirohi) capacity raised from 500 to 1,500 KLPD; cumulative capacity about 4,80,000 KL per year. Management says industrial sales are rising after ARAI certifications, and the company has three plants: two in Padgol, Gujarat and one in Sirohi, Rajasthan.

segments.name: Glycerin and byproducts
segments.commentary: Management cited glycerin as a byproduct monetised across pharma, food, cosmetics, personal care and paint; no volume or revenue figures were given.

segments.name: FMCG
segments.commentary: Analyst asked about recently launched FMCG products; management said they are doing well across all markets, with no figures given.

guidance_outlook: Utilisation to improve gradually towards 60-70% over the next few years, per management.
Near-term growth of 15-20%, possibly up to 30%, with at least 15% expected; management said revenue and utilisation growth would be roughly in line.
Management said margins would improve a little as utilisation rises, but gave no quantified margin target.

Two new 200 KLPD plants at Jhajjar (Haryana) and Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh) expected to be commissioned by December 2026, adding 400 KLPD (about 75% increase in capacity per management), funded from internal accruals.
Management targets 60-80% growth over the next four to five years.

Biodiesel exports: management said an export licence would take four to six months, with a Padgol or Sirohi unit converted to an EOU and ISCC certification pending; the call gave conflicting timelines and export revenue was said to arrive 'this year'.
risks_watch: Margin compression: the analyst cited a drop from about 15% to 8-10% operating margin; management did not reconcile the two figures.
Utilisation at 7-8% against a 1,500 KLPD plant and the 400 KLPD expansion; growth depends on OMC tenders and industrial demand.
Policy risk: an isobutanol blending plan was mentioned by the minister; management called it unviable on price and said the government favours ethanol.
Legal matters: the promoter's seized-raw-material case (next hearing next month) and the Supreme Court penalty matter with no timeline; a Rajasthan registration renewal is pending.
Export timing is unclear: management gave a 4-6 month licence timeline and also said revenue would arrive 'this year' and in Q1; ISCC certification is still pending.

Governance and disclosure: management declined a factory visit and some answers were evasive or unclear (asset turnover, employee plans); promoter share sales were described as being used to reduce debt towards zero-debt.
Feedstock: management said it uses 10-15 non-edible feedstocks and does not use used cooking oil (UCO).
544726|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity, but vague and sometimes inconsistent on specifics such as margins, export timelines, utilisation and asset turnover, which management deferred. Management was defensive on policy questions and declined to comment on the isobutanol plan.
key_quotes: We are also setting two new biodiesel manufacturing facility at Jhajjar in Haryana and Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh, each with a capacity of 200 KLPD.
Management remains confident of improving utilization level gradually over the next few years towards 60 to 70%.
Kotyark Industries achieves a yield of more than 99%, and that is also one of our strengths.
No, I am reducing debt. I am taking the company towards a zero-debt position.

Execution expected over next three months

financial_highlights.change: Figure raised by analyst; not confirmed by management

qa_highlights.question: Why are OMCs not increasing biodiesel tender quantity and blending despite higher crude prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it depends on government policy and OMC requirements and blending will keep rising gradually.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current operating margin given the move in OMC rates, and why did it fall from about 15% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current margins are 8-10%, that raw material cost moves with OMC rates so the margin is unchanged, and that it manages costs so PAT is not significantly affected; it did not reconcile the 15% figure.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue and utilisation grow by 15-20%, and will margins hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue and utilisation growth would be roughly in line at 15-20%, possibly up to 30%, with at least 15% expected; margins would improve a little as utilisation rises.

qa_highlights.question: When can exports start and will revenue come in FY27 or FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the export licence takes four to six months, one of the Padgol or Sirohi units would be converted to an EOU, and ISCC certification is pending; it said export revenue would come 'this year itself'.

qa_highlights.question: What is the asset turnover expected at the Sirohi plant at normal utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an asset turnover figure; it gave Rs 3,500-4,000 crore as the revenue at optimum utilisation and said it would explain asset turnover later.

qa_highlights.question: Is the promoter share sale being used to fund the new plants, and what is the debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the proceeds stayed in Kotyark, it took nothing personally, and the sale was to reduce debt, with the aim of a zero-debt position.

capex_capacity: Rajasthan (Sirohi) biodiesel capacity raised from 500 to 1,500 KLPD in FY26; cumulative annual capacity about 4,80,000 KL; management expects utilisation to rise gradually to 60-70% over next few years from current 7-8%.

Two new 200 KLPD biodiesel plants at Jhajjar (Haryana) and Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh), total 400 KLPD, expected commissioning by December 2026; management said this is about a 75% capacity increase; funded from internal accruals.

No capex amount disclosed for the Jhajjar and Kanpur plants; management said plant cost is about one-fourth of peers' Rs 250-300 crore investment for 300-350 KLPD plants, but gave no figure for the new projects.
Existing storage judged sufficient; no additional storage or depot plans; company uses own vehicles for finished goods delivery.
Management declined a factory plant visit, offering an office visit instead.
demand_pricing: Demand driver cited: OMC blending tenders; analyst said an earlier tender ran at about 5 crore litres per month and a current tender for 15 crore litres over three months has been issued, and asked why OMCs are not raising blending; management said it follows government policy and OMC requirements and will increase gradually.
OMC tender allocation has moved from location-based to total-quantity-based; management said the company only needs to fulfil quantity, and previously it bid in locations where it was not L1.

Pricing: management said raw material cost moves with OMC rates, so a lower rate leaves margin unchanged; at current rates operating margin is 8-10% (analyst had cited about 15% in FY26; management said margins have improved in industrial sales without disclosing price).

Industrial demand: management said industrial sales are rising after ARAI certifications for mining and generator operators; industrial diesel reportedly around Rs 140 per litre per analyst, price not disclosed by management.
Customers named by management: sells biodiesel to Modern Insulators and semi-finished biodiesel to E-Diesel Biofuels; management said it can supply raw or semi-finished material to competitors.

Exports: management said biodiesel export is currently banned and a licence is being obtained; the company needs one of its Padgol or Sirohi plants converted to an EOU and ISCC certification, which is in process.

Glycerin: management cited monetisation across pharmaceuticals, foods, cosmetics, personal care and paint; no volume or revenue numbers given. Vera carbon certification with over 57,000 carbon credits generated.
Order book: executable order book of about Rs 80 crore from OMCs and other customers, expected to execute over the next three months; pipeline of about Rs 215 crore.
Feedstock: management said it uses 10-15 non-edible oils and does not make biodiesel from used cooking oil, citing higher cost and lower yield.
Geography: current focus is North India; management said it may later expand to Maharashtra; no plans for southern expansion stated.

544733|2026-06.headline: GSP Crop Science Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR386 crore (from INR377 crore) and PAT grew about 16% to INR26.4 crore, helped by a one-off land sale gain.
544733|2026-06.overview: Revenue was broadly stable at INR386 crore versus INR377 crore in the prior-year quarter, with strong domestic momentum partly offset by raw material constraints in international business. Gross margin improved on a richer mix of specialty and patented products, and EBITDA was stated at around 11%. PAT rose almost 16% to INR26.4 crore, but management said about INR5.7 crore of other income came from a land sale, which is a one-off. ICRA upgraded the long-term rating from A to A+ stable, citing IPO-funded debt repayment and performance.

segments.name: Domestic B2C (branded)
segments.commentary: About 45% of Q1 revenue. Patented products are about 20-22% of B2C sales; management aims to roughly double this over 3 years. Recent launches PCT 410 and Fighter are gaining volume.

segments.name: Domestic B2B
segments.commentary: About 45% of Q1 revenue. Co-marketing of patented products with B2B partners showed good growth. Management targets B2B at 30-35% of revenue over the next 3 years.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: About 10% of Q1 revenue, seasonally weighted to H2 (Latin America, mainly Brazil). Q1 hit by raw material constraints, order slippage to China, and Brazil credit and liquidity concerns. Expected to be about 20% of mix over 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 15% growth rate, with EBITDA growing 13-14% over the next 2-3 years (earlier in the call, EBITDA margin guidance of 12-13% was given).

Management expects the Q2 season to track anticipated growth; PAT in Q2 is expected to be a similar share of full-year PAT as last year (Q2 FY26 was about 60% of full-year PAT), with the absolute number higher.
Management expects Brazil demand to recover from September for H2 ahead of the October season.
Management targets a domestic market share rise from about 3-3.5% to 7-8%.

Management says patented product share of the portfolio will double in 2-3 years, with about 12 products launched in the last 3 years and two to three new patented formulations and one or two technicals a year.
capex_capacity: Technical capacity utilisation is about 70-75%, with room to grow and scope to swap high-value, low-volume products in multi-product plants.
Formulation plant utilisation is about 25-30%; management says formulations are sized for peak season and are not a bottleneck.
Backward-integration technical plant at Dahej and Saykha was capitalised after the prior quarter, raising depreciation.
Technical plant can run 12 months to supply H2 export demand from Latin America.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices were volatile in Q1 due to geopolitical events and petrochemical-linked inputs. Rupee depreciation of about 10-11% also raised input costs. Management said B2B prices can be passed on, while B2C has a lag covered by inventory.
Demand was held back by price volatility, with farmers, channel partners and formulators delaying purchases. Management cited El Nino forecasts and crude volatility.
Monsoon rains from July were good; cotton and soybean acreage is up and chillies are increasing. Management expects insecticide and fungicide demand to benefit.

Brazil demand is weak with customer liquidity and credit issues, and some orders moved to China on logistics. Management is cautious and is focusing on established B2B partners and second-tier distributors in Argentina and Uruguay.
Management says farmers are moving to specialty molecules and preventive spraying. It cited West Bengal as an example.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mix between technicals, formulations and branded patented products?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel mix is about 45% B2C, 45% B2B and 10% export. Formulations are about 75% and technicals about 25%. Patented products are about 20-22% of B2C, with a target to double over 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of IPO fund utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The loan repayment object has been fully met during the quarter. A small residual amount remains pending bank settlement of brokerage, which may take 2-3 months, before the IPO account can be closed.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material costs affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expansion is mainly from product mix. Rupee depreciation of 10-11% and petrochemical-linked price volatility raised input costs. B2B passes costs through, and B2C is covered by inventory for now.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Q1 export business faring and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Brazil orders were delayed by pricing volatility and some shifted to China. Management expects destocking, with demand returning from September for the October season. It is pursuing Argentina and Uruguay via second-tier distributors and new registrations.

qa_highlights.question: How is Kharif progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: July rains were good and key kharif acreage is up. Management said South India (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka) is still a wait-and-watch situation based on monsoon. No material shortage is seen currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Technical utilisation is about 70-75% with scope to add high-value products. Formulation utilisation is about 25-30%, which management says is by design for peak-season capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The company plans one or two new technicals a year, with data generation taking 4-5 years, and two to three new patented formulations a year, with a pipeline covering the next 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off nature of other income and the outlook for it?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR5.7 crore of the INR8.3 crore other income is the land-sale gain. No further other income is planned for the remaining quarters. Management said the land sale is a one-off.

risks_watch: Other income of about INR5.7 crore from a one-off land sale inflated Q1 PAT. Excluding it, management's PAT growth looks much lower, and the analyst cited roughly flat PBT.
Raw material volatility and rupee depreciation of 10-11% could compress B2C margins if pass-through lags.
Brazil credit and liquidity stress, plus loss of orders to China on logistics, puts export recovery at risk. Export is about 10% of Q1 revenue.
South India (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka) depends on monsoon, and the El Nino forecast adds uncertainty.
Management guidance is inconsistent: EBITDA margin 12-13% in one answer, EBITDA growth 13-14% in another, and PAT growth expectations are not quantified. Monitor Q2 delivery against these.

544735|2026-03.headline: Novus Loyalty FY26 revenue rose about 22% to ~127 Cr, with PAT of ~9.28 Cr (7.29% margin) in its first results call after its 25 March 2026 listing.
544735|2026-03.overview: Novus Loyalty, a B2B2C loyalty and engagement technology company, reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) revenue of about 127 Cr, up roughly 22% YoY. EBITDA was about 12.33 Cr (9.68% margin) and PAT about 9.28 Cr (7.29% margin), with management citing PAT growth of about 150% and EBITDA growth of about 120%. Management attributed margin improvement to programs maturing (redemptions rising in years 2 to 3) and a shift toward technology and merchant-promotion revenue, which carry no direct procurement cost. Management guided to growth above 20% in FY27 and to international revenue at least doubling, but gave no formal numerical guidance, and the call was largely promotional with limited hard data.

financial_highlights.change: listed 25 March 2026; no proceeds utilised in FY26

segments.name: Technology
segments.commentary: Enterprise platform set-up fee and the first revenue line to open with a client; management says it carries no direct cost and is the main focus. Cited Central Bank order worth 88 Cr (via GeM) and Bank of Abyssinia technology revenue of about 4 Cr.

segments.name: Redemption
segments.commentary: Second revenue line, opening after technology in BFSI programs; carries a direct procurement cost. Management cited a client where redeeming customers rose from about 10,000 to 10 lakh within 10 months.

segments.name: Merchant promotions
segments.commentary: Merchants fund accelerated campaigns and pay affiliate commissions, which management said run at about 8-10% of tracked spend, of which part is passed to customers. Described as a higher-margin line with no direct cost.

segments.name: Digital vouchers
segments.commentary: Fourth line; vouchers sourced partly from vendors such as Gyftr. Carries direct procurement cost. Management said the voucher line is about 5% of Gyftr's business in its comparison.

guidance_outlook: Management said FY27 growth will be above 20%, but gave no revenue number.

International revenue to at least double from about 3.3 Cr in FY26, 'if not triple'. Management cited about 5 Cr for FY27 and more than 6 Cr in one answer, then 'close to 10' / 'more than 10' for FY27-28, which is internally inconsistent.
India growth expected at 15-20%.
Margins expected to rise from current levels as the mix shifts toward technology and merchant promotion.
IPO proceeds planned as about 11-12 Cr for sales and business development (about half in FY27), about 10-12 Cr for product development and AI, and about 12 Cr for small acquisitions.
Bank accounts onboarded recently, such as Central Bank, are expected to reach peak levels in FY27, which management said could increase numbers by 100%.
capex_capacity: Planned UAE wholly owned subsidiary, expected to be finalised in about a month; physical presence to serve MENA clients.
Two partners onboarded in Africa, with workshops started; Bank of Abyssinia (Ethiopia) order is the first such contract.

Planned acquisition of a small marketing agency or digital agency in the US and Australia, targeted this year or next, subject to finding the right candidate. Management also cited a PPI licence as a possible acquisition target.
Hiring additional sales staff in India for channel partner and corporate loyalty programs; management said BFSI needs no extra staff.
Platform scales from 10,000 to 100 million customers, with SaaS launch in about 2-3 weeks and on-premise deployment for banks.
demand_pricing: Over 100 enterprise customers and more than 4 crore end-customers on the platform; about 50 crore transactions processed per month; about 80 employees.
Clients include NPCI (since 2019), Central Bank, IDBI, Bank of Maharashtra, Equitas Bank, Sparkle Bank (Nigeria), PRYPCO (DAMAC) and NovaDisk (healthcare, 3 countries).
Contracts run 3-5 years with 3-5 year renewals (6-10 year total tenure). Programs typically mature in year 3, and management said margins rise over the program life.
Competition: management named Salesforce and other large loyalty players in the Bank of Abyssinia tender; said its platform processes transactions in 8 hours versus 24 hours for others.
Redemption rates in Indian bank programs are about 10%, against 45-50% in the US and Australia, which management cited as upside.
Management said seasonality has a 5-10% effect, mainly around September-October festive months.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth exceed 20% in FY27, and what revenue is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth would be 'more than' 20% and that IPO-funded sales and international expansion would grow the business faster than FY26, but gave no revenue figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ~10% margins sustainable, or were there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would increase from current levels as technology and merchant promotion revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: How will IPO proceeds be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately 11-12 Cr for business development and sales, about 10-12 Cr for product development and AI, and about 12 Cr for small acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Does Novus keep breakage on expired points, and what about gift points?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Novus is B2B2C and breakage goes to the bank client; it does not hold a PPI licence, so it cannot keep breakage. Management said Indian bank points expiry is about 7-10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international revenue mix and reseller economics?
qa_highlights.answer: International revenue was about 2.6% of FY26 revenue (about 3.3 Cr). Resellers take about 15-30% of the deal value depending on local support needs, and Novus retains IP ownership.

qa_highlights.question: How does Novus compare with Zaggle and Gyftr?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Zaggle focuses on spend management and employee rewards, which are about 5-10% of Novus's business. Gyftr is a voucher vendor to Novus, not a loyalty competitor.

risks_watch: Growth depends on the timing of program maturity and on contract wins, including government/GeM tenders that management said can be cancelled or uneven (Canara order cancelled).
International expansion relies on partners, resellers and a planned US/Australia acquisition, with reseller margins of 15-30% and a licence-dependent PPI plan that is not yet in place.
The FY27 international revenue guidance is internally inconsistent (about 5 Cr, then more than 6 Cr, then 10 Cr or more), so the number needs confirmation.
Concentration in BFSI and a few large bank and government clients; redemption-driven revenue carries direct procurement cost.
Use of IPO proceeds (about 60 Cr raised) has not yet been reported; watch quarterly deployment and the outcome of the planned acquisition.
Management did not give FY26 comparatives in detail; the EBITDA and PAT growth figures (120%, 150%) are management's approximations.

544735|2026-09.headline: Novus Loyalty H1 FY27 revenue rose to about ₹98 crore (vs ₹71 crore in H1 FY26), with ~35-40% growth; AutoPay 80.87% acquisition pending funding in June 2027.

544740|2026-03.headline: Tipco FY26 total income rose 9.5% to INR146 crore, with H2 income up 66% to INR95 crore and PAT up 65% to INR25.31 crore.

Total income was INR146 crore versus INR133 crore, and H2 income reached INR95 crore against INR57 crore in the corresponding period. EBITDA rose 62% to INR38.9 crore, with margin at 26.63% versus 17.95%, and PAT rose 65% to INR25.31 crore with a 17.32% margin. Management guided to Pune plant contributing toward INR180 crore total revenue in FY27, with 25% capacity in FY27, 75% in FY28, and full capacity in about two years. Debtor days rose sharply from 72 to 169, which management attributed to higher H2 sales.

544741|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14.5% to INR16.11 crore and PAT rose 66.9% to INR4.10 crore, with management guiding FY27 revenue of INR30-32 crore.
544741|2026-03.overview: Highness Microelectronics reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) as its strongest year since listing on BSE SME: revenue INR16.11 crore (+14.5% YoY), EBITDA INR6.61 crore (+46%), and PAT INR4.10 crore (+66.9%). Management attributed margin gains to favourable project mix and high-margin contracts, and said H2 has historically been stronger than H1. Growth plans centre on a Goa facility for COG/FOG display manufacturing, a glass cutting line at Rabale, and an MoU with Axiom (USA). Management did not give a clean H2 standalone revenue figure, and several answers on order book and margins were loosely quantified.

544742|2026-03.headline: Sai Parenterals Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue INR198 crore with 15% EBITDA margin; FY27 guided to INR750 crore revenue at 17% EBITDA margin.

rows.label: Working capital absorbs 25-30% of incremental revenue
rows.why: Management expects working capital at 25-30% of incremental revenue; on the INR750 cr target versus INR381 cr FY26 base, that is cash pressure on INR319 cr total debt, partly offset by long-term CDMO contracts with shorter receivable cycles.

rows.label: Debt peak in FY27, decline from FY28

544742|2026-06.headline: Sai Parenterals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 182 crore, EBITDA margin 14.9%; IPO funds Rs 101.85 crore redeployed to a 60% stake in Saicriti.

PAT was Rs 8 crore (4.3% margin), down from Rs 13.2 crore in Q4 on a normalised tax charge and lower revenue. The Board approved varying IPO objects, moving Rs 83.83 crore from Jeedimetla upgrades to a 60% stake in Saicriti Pharma and Rs 18.02 crore from a greenfield R&D centre to a 60% stake in Prathyak Laboratories (Rs 15 crore), both subject to shareholder approval. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of Rs 750 crore revenue at about 17% EBITDA margin, weighted to H2.

segments.name: Noumed Pharmaceuticals (Australia/NZ)
segments.commentary: Consolidated since 12 Nov 2025; Q1 revenue was hit by West Asia shipping delays, forcing air freight and extra regulatory costs. Renewed EBOS (TerryWhite Chemmart, Pharmacy Choice) OTC contract from 1 July 2026, valued at AUD 202 million (about Rs 1,300 crore) over 7.5 years, roughly AUD 27 million a year.

segments.name: Standalone (India, injectables and exports)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue Rs 56 crore with EBITDA margin about 29%, attributed mainly to operating leverage. Current exports are only oral dosage and cephalosporins; domestic injectables dominate Units 1 and 2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reiterated: revenue Rs 750 crore and EBITDA margin about 17%, with a 45:55 H1:H2 split (CFO-era statement also referred to 44:55 in Q&A).
Q1 revenue is said to be about 24% of the full-year Rs 750 crore target, ahead of the phasing needed.
Noumed Australia contribution from the EBOS renewal begins in Q2 FY27.
Management expects the recovery of raw material cost increases to flow through the contract book over Q2 as the 90-120 day price-revision lag unwinds.
FY27 described as a building year; FY28 expected to show the impact. No FY28 number given; management will decide at Q3 call.
Management expects peak debt in FY27 with de-leveraging from FY28.
capex_capacity: Saicriti Pharma (60% stake, Rs 83.83 crore, total project cost about Rs 215-217 crore): critical care injectable facility at Gummadidala, outside the outer ring road, over 15,000 sq yd; completion extended to about April 2027; about 154.66 million units of capacity vs about 105 million under the original Jeedimetla upgrade (about 47% more).
Jeedimetla Units 1 and 2 (about 3,100 sq yd) cannot be expanded and fall within the outer ring road, where upgrades are no longer permitted under HILTP policy.
Prathyak Laboratories (60%, Rs 15 crore): R&D centre at Genome Valley, Hyderabad, expected to complete on or before 30 September 2026; to be renamed Sai Prathyak as a step-down subsidiary.

Australia (Noumed) facility: AUD 53 million total programme funding now complete; physical completion targeted January 2027, TGA inspection by March 2027, Phase 1 manufacturing from April 2027. Packing-line validation through December-February.

Local manufacture is expected to cut Noumed inventory from 9-10 months to about 5-6 months of stock; one Indian container of inputs replaces 8 finished-goods containers. Federal Modern Manufacturing Initiative grant of AUD 20 million cited.
demand_pricing: Noumed holds 5 exclusive long-term contracts and 10 exclusive supply molecule contracts covering 526 SKUs, typically 5+ years.
Wesfarmers Health and EBOS networks together cover over 2,900 of about 5,500 Australian pharmacies.

EBOS contract: about 12 new products per year targeted; first 24 NPD products identified, with 8 to be developed by Sai's R&D (6 started), 4 exclusive supply contracts and the rest via a Catalent soft-gel partnership.
Management said pharmacy-channel growth for some molecules is running at about 8%, and that more order wins of similar size should come over the next year.
Prathyak pipeline: 150 SKUs across 86 molecules (lyophilised, liposomal, nano-based, oncology and critical-care injectables).
Management stated the injectables export plan targets Europe, Southeast Asia, Latin America and the Middle East first, with the US to be reviewed later.
Saicriti existing domestic critical care franchise about Rs 52-53 crore, currently produced via CMOs and to move to the new site.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 12 new NPD products included in the AUD 202 million EBOS order value, and should more order wins of similar size be expected over the next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Mark Thulborne said the NPD products sit on top of the order value, which reflects the existing supply portfolio. He said more order wins of this size should come over the next year, with pharmacy-network growth of about 5-8% a year.

qa_highlights.question: Given the many parallel initiatives (Noumed integration, capacity, R&D, US entry), how is management bandwidth protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Anil K K said Sai is retaining the existing Noumed management, which holds 25.4% of Noumed, and the 4 senior Prathyak managers, with Sai providing manufacturing, funding and procurement support.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire 60% of a new facility rather than upgrade Jeedimetla as originally planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a Telangana government order that red and orange category units must move out of the outer ring road, which blocked upgrades at Units 1 and 2. Jeedimetla is about 3,100 sq yd against the 12,000-13,000 sq yd an EU-GMP plant needs, and a greenfield start would take 6-8 months just for land and approvals.

qa_highlights.question: What incremental products and markets will the new facility unlock, and why is there a pricing decline in injectables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first targets are Europe, Southeast Asia, Latin America and the Middle East, with the US to be reviewed later. Historically Units 1 and 2 served domestic injectables only, while exports were limited to oral dosage and cephalosporins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saicriti shareholding and the related-party status, and what are the funding details?
qa_highlights.answer: Saicriti is not a related party, per management. Critigen Pharma, with its subsidiary Questus Pharma, holds the remaining 40%, around Rs 56 crore, with the balance funded through project debt on a total project cost of about Rs 217 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 margin decline from Noumed a one-off, and is the guidance upgrade possible?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the Noumed cost hit was one-time, from West Asia supply constraints that drove extra freight and regulatory costs. Management reiterated Rs 750 crore revenue and about 17% EBITDA for FY27, declined to give an FY28 number, and will revisit at Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt trajectory and peak debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was about Rs 310 crore at 30 June 2026 versus about Rs 320 crore in March 2026, after repaying about Rs 50 crore of loans from IPO proceeds. Management expects peak debt in FY27, with gross debt-to-equity around 0.6 times even at peak, and de-leveraging from FY28.

Noumed Australia: the Q2 gross margin recovery depends on raw material price pass-through (90-120 day lag) and the EBOS renewal starting in Q2 FY27.
Australian facility timelines: physical completion January 2027, TGA inspection by March 2027, Phase 1 manufacturing from April 2027.
FY27 H2 weighting: Rs 750 crore revenue needs a steep ramp after Q1 at about 24% of target; the H1:H2 split is quoted as both 45:55 and 44:55.
Debt peak in FY27 with new project debt added at subsidiary level, and the US subsidiary is at a preliminary evaluation stage with no tax or capex details.
Q1 PAT fell to Rs 8 crore from Rs 13.2 crore in Q4 on a normalised tax charge, and consolidated revenue declined QoQ.
key_quotes: I would emphasize that this improvement was achieved on a lower revenue base, and it was achieved despite absorbing elevated air freight cost in Australia.
The purpose for which the IPO funds were raised namely European GMP compliant injectable capacity for regulated markets and a dedicated research and development platform remains entirely unchanged.
FY '27 remains a year of building. FY '28 is when the build should start showing in our performance.
Now, it is too premature to discuss this part because now the US subsidiary whichever we are going to, which we took the permission from the board to start a US subsidiary.

544744|2026-03.headline: Powerica FY26 revenue crossed INR3,012 crore (+13.5% YoY) and EBITDA margin was 12.8%; management targets double-digit FY27 top-line growth.
544744|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR801 crore (+10.9% YoY) with EBITDA of INR86 crore (10.8% margin) and PAT of INR45 crore (5.6% margin). Full-year FY26 PAT of INR277 crore (9.2% margin) was helped by a INR51 crore deferred tax credit from a tax regime change. Management said the IPO-related debt repayment of INR525 crore should cut finance costs from Q1 FY27, and cash including investments was about INR450 crore as of May 26. Management flagged geopolitical tensions, energy prices and supply-chain pressure as weighing on near-term demand, especially in Q1 FY27, and said margin pressure seen in Q4 is temporary.

segments.name: DG Sets (Cummins-powered)
segments.commentary: About 83% of FY26 revenue with 10.9% YoY growth and 9.1% EBITDA margin; Cummins-powered DG sets were about 66% of revenue. Data centers were about 12% of the Cummins business, and high-horsepower sets were over 50% of value.

segments.name: MSLG (medium-speed large generators)
segments.commentary: About 5% of FY26 revenue. Project-driven, with revenue tied to execution milestones and project cycles of 12 to 48 months, so management wants it judged over multiple quarters. The Australia project is 90-95% complete.

segments.name: Allied businesses
segments.commentary: EMI shelters, containers, defence applications, acoustic enclosures, Schneider Electric Prisma panels and project work; about 12.5% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Wind (IPP, EPC, O&M for BoP)
segments.commentary: INR512 crore in FY26 (16.9% of revenue), +28.6% YoY with 31.3% EBITDA margin. IPP is about 40% and EPC/O&M about 60% of wind revenue. Owns 12 Gujarat projects with 330.85 MW installed.

segments.name: Platino Automotive (associate)
segments.commentary: Retrofit emission control device (RECD) for pre-CPCB4+ DG sets of 125 kVA and above, cutting emissions by up to 92%; device cost INR3-30 lakh per installation. FY26 was a marketing-infrastructure build year; Q4 sales INR22 crore and PBT INR5.8 crore.

guidance_outlook: Targeting double-digit top-line growth in FY27.
DG sets organic growth target of about 11-12% in FY27, against an industry growth estimate of about 10.5%.
Management expects margins to recover, with the 50 MW wind capacity contributing from Q2 FY27 and higher wind generation in the first two quarters.
Finance cost to fall substantially from Q1 FY27 after debt repayment, which should lift PAT margin.
Revenue mix expected to move to about 75-80% gensets and 20-25% wind, with the EBITDA mix shifting further toward wind.
Depreciation to rise in FY27 as another 50 MW is capitalised, with about INR400 crore of EPC BoP business expected each year.
capex_capacity: Wind IPP portfolio: 12 Gujarat projects at 330.85 MW installed; a further 52.7 MW project under construction takes it to about 384 MW at completion.
Secured 100 MW of GUVNL bids at Botad, with another 50 MW at advanced planning stage.
Khavda 2 GW RE project with GE Vernova JV is on hold pending land allotment from the Gujarat government.
FY26 capex was 51.3 MW for the business. MSLG needs no capex, as it is a service model.
Manufacturing in Bangalore, Silvassa and Khopoli; everything except the engine and alternator is made in-house.
demand_pricing: Data center demand is strong, with an order book of 9 months to about a year of work and continuing inquiries, which management says rose after the budget.
EPC BoP order book is about 585 MW, including 175 MW in Gujarat (completion expected by Dec 2026) and 410 MW for Torrent Power in Maharashtra; orders run to about Dec 2027.
Wind IPP PPAs are 25-year, fixed-tariff contracts with GUVNL and SECI.
EPC installation work on data centers ranges from 25% to 75% of the supply order value.
Competitive pressure is rising in wind through ROW and land constraints, per management.
Management did not name data center competitors and said it could not quantify the data center share of hyperscaler capex.

qa_highlights.question: What were Platino's Q4 revenue and PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Deferred to a later point in the call; Ritesh Agrawal then said Q4 FY26 Platino sales were INR22 crore with PBT of INR5.8 crore (PAT not given).

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins stay at about 10.5% in FY27 after the softer Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the Q3/Q4 dip temporary, citing geopolitical tensions, and expects FY27 to be in target range. It expects better margins from Q2 onward, helped by the 50 MW wind capacity and higher wind generation in the first two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are wind EPC/O&M inquiries facing land and connectivity delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradeep Gupta said the order book covers 585 MW to about Dec 2027, so there is enough work in hand. The 175 MW Gujarat project should complete by Dec 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Khavda 2 GW project timeline and the ROW situation?
qa_highlights.answer: The Khavda project is a long-term JV with GE Vernova and is still waiting for land from the Gujarat government. ROW issues are not improving, as competition and RE investment grow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IPP EBITDA margin and PLF?
qa_highlights.answer: The portfolio's EBITDA margin is about 60-62%. New machines run at 36.5% PLF and older ones at 23-24%, with an average of about 26% across the roughly 280 MW profile. New projects earn about 87-88% EBITDA in year one, stabilising at 82-83%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue split between EPC and IPP, and what growth drivers are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: IPP capacity will grow each year as projects are added, while EPC BoP work of about INR400 crore a year (250-300 MW) is steady. Growth drivers cited are data centers, manufacturing, realty, EV charging backup and rental. Over four to five years the revenue mix is expected at about 75:25 gensets to wind.

qa_highlights.question: How does Powerica view competition from fuel-cell technology such as Bloom Energy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would deliver any new technology to market and that gensets stay as backup for 20-25 years. Jai Ram Oberoi said the company is a power solutions provider, not only a DG set maker.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DG set growth outlook, split between price and volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic DG growth target is about 11-12% for FY27, with MSLG contributing on a milestone basis. Management did not split price from volume.

qa_highlights.question: Is Platino expected to grow faster than DG sets?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Jai Ram Oberoi said Platino is a small, high-growth business supported by state-level mandates, and FY26 was spent building marketing infrastructure.

Khavda 2 GW project is held up until the Gujarat government allots land; no timeline was given.
Right-of-way and land constraints in wind are unlikely to ease and are raising competition for sites.
FY26 PAT was helped by a INR51 crore deferred tax credit, so the underlying PAT margin is lower than the reported 9.2%.
Data center exposure is about 12% of revenue; management would not name competitors or quantify the share of hyperscaler capex.
Platino's contribution is small (Q4 sales INR22 crore) and depends on enforcement of state-level RECD mandates.
MSLG revenue is lumpy because it depends on milestones over 12-48 months.

544744|2026-06.headline: Powerica Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26.7% YoY to INR780 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 13.6% on commodity inflation; DC order book hit INR900 crore (INR1,100 crore by Aug 7).
544744|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 26.7% YoY to INR780 crore, with EBITDA of INR106 crore (13.6% margin) and PAT of INR64 crore (8.3% margin). Management said elevated commodity and energy prices, a lag in passing costs to customers, and an adverse revenue mix compressed genset margins, with recovery expected from Q2-Q3 after two-phase price hikes. Order book as of July 31, 2026 was INR1,700 crore, of which data center orders were INR900 crore. Wind IPP portfolio visibility rose to about 638 MW after new awards, and FY27 double-digit revenue growth guidance was reiterated.

segments.name: DG sets (Cummins-powered)
segments.commentary: Order book of INR1,700 crore as of July 31, 2026, with data center orders at INR900 crore; genset EBITDA margin fell to 5.6% in Q1 on commodity costs and mix. Capacity utilisation 75-80% on one shift.

segments.name: Wind / IPP and EPC-BOP
segments.commentary: Wind is 18.6% of revenue, growing 28.8% YoY at a 48.6% EBITDA margin, helped by 51.3 MW added in Feb 2026. Owned IPP capacity is 330 MW, with a roadmap to about 638 MW.

segments.name: MSLG (defence/large projects)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell on slower order booking because international inquiries were put on hold by the geopolitical situation. Won a INR41 crore tender to be executed in 12-15 months and has a large PSU order executable by Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Allied business
segments.commentary: Contributed 9% of revenue; management attributed the slowdown to milestone-based project revenue recognition and defence product approval cycles of 1-3 years.

Order book up 15-19% YoY as of July 31, 2026, depending on product mix.
Data center order book expected to execute over 12-18 months; management expects data center at 20%+ of revenue on an annualised basis.
Wind pipeline: 50 MW to go live in Q4 FY27, 150 MW in FY28, and 100 MW the year after.

qa_highlights.question: Genset margin outlook and whether the order book is fixed-price?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are impacted by the West Asia crisis for Q1 and part of Q2, improving from Q3. Older orders have fixed prices, with some price hikes obtained; new orders carry new prices.

qa_highlights.question: Data center BOP share and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: BOP execution is about 30% of data center project value. Margins vary order to order by volume, delivery timeline, engine requirement and customisation; no fixed margin given.

qa_highlights.question: DG capacity utilisation and expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 75-80% on one shift; current capacity is sufficient, with expansion planned if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Wind PPA timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: 100 MW GUVNL PPA signed and under construction. The 50 MW GUVNL PPA is expected by Nov-Dec 2026 after LOA and about 90 days. The 100 MW SECI PPA is pending SECI's call.

qa_highlights.question: Wind EBITDA margins by project type?
qa_highlights.answer: New projects earn 82-83% EBITDA per management, old 330 MW projects 62-63%, EPC 10-11%. Analysts noted these figures as stated by management.

risks_watch: Genset margin (5.6% in Q1) recovery depends on whether price hikes stick over one or two quarters amid high commodity and energy prices.
Old data center orders were priced before the hikes, so margin may stay below the new-order level until they execute.
MSLG order inflow slowed because international inquiries were paused by the geopolitical situation; the pipeline is not yet quantified.
Wind PPAs for the 50 MW GUVNL and 100 MW SECI projects are still pending, and commissioning depends on them.
Competition in data centers is rising, and management said it lost two direct data center projects to Cummins in the past (per analyst).

financial_highlights.metric: EPC and O&M for BOP share

financial_highlights.change: Lower; demand deferred by crisis and GRAP

So quantum has been there over the period, so it's right now if I would say the 10%, 15%, it is not right.

544748|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 129% YoY to INR 158.3 crore, driven by first full quarter of Netcom BCC, with EBITDA margin at 24.9%.
544748|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full reporting period consolidating Netcom BCC, lifting consolidated revenue to INR 158.3 crore (up 64.6% QoQ, 129% YoY) and EBITDA to INR 39.4 crore (24.9% margin). Profit for the period rose to INR 16.3 crore, with basic EPS of 0.62 versus 0.36 a year ago. Finance cost rose to INR 8.1 crore from INR 1.9 crore, tied to acquisition borrowing. Management positioned the company as moving from capacity-led outsourcing toward outcome-based AI orchestration through its ResolX platform, while the standalone base business grew 11.6% YoY.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1.9 crore a year ago

financial_highlights.value: ~50% of revenue and ~50% of EBITDA; Netcom margin ~24-25%

segments.name: Global human service engine (incl. Netcom BCC)
segments.commentary: Netcom fully consolidated this quarter, deepening Americas presence; contributes roughly half of consolidated revenue and EBITDA at ~24-25% margin.

segments.name: Base business (standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue INR 61.1 crore, up 11.6% YoY, at 30.4% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Agentic AI engine (ResolX)
segments.commentary: Launched May 2026; 12 live deployments across seven enterprise clients. Revenue described as only just starting to catch up; management expects meaningful revenue in 12-18 months or slightly more.

guidance_outlook: Management said the company should be able to roughly double revenue this year, while acknowledging this was not a one-off quarter.
Management expects EBITDA margins to improve progressively over the coming year as the revenue mix shifts to AI orchestration and outcome-linked models.
Cash generation expected to rise in coming quarters, making debt servicing easier; no equity raise indicated.
Management intends to acquire two more companies over the next three years, targeting firms with Fortune 500 clients in North America.
AI-led revenue expected to show up in quarterly numbers over the coming 12-18 months.
capex_capacity: Netcom BCC acquisition debt carries an effective cost of around 9%; management said total debt is about INR 220 crore and a repayment schedule is planned.

ResolX platform: 12 live deployments across seven enterprise clients (insurance, aviation, banking, automotive, digital assets), including two Central American banks; management said about 6-7 of 12 projects were deployed as of the call.
Management plans roughly 40-plus bots for one Indian insurance client across languages and its 7-8 products.
Management said capacity is not a constraint, with AI expected to free room in accounts for additional work.
demand_pricing: Management expects growth from India and LATAM, with the Americas growing on dollar arbitrage; banking is the leading vertical, with some insurance, healthcare, travel and hospitality.
AI deflection to humans reported at roughly 30-40% depending on use case; one airline deployment cited about 30% of employee-size benefit.
Management claims the company is the only Indian BPO with in-house domain, tech stack and Agentic AI capabilities; other BPOs described as relying on third-party AI.
Conversion rate on active deal pipeline stated at around 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the current quarter's run rate one-off or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not one-off, as this is the first quarter with full Netcom consolidation, and it expects revenue to roughly double this year.

qa_highlights.question: Split of revenue and EBITDA between Netcom and base business, and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Netcom contributes about 50% of revenue and about 50% of EBITDA, with margins of 24-25%, similar to group margin.

qa_highlights.question: Plan for INR 220 crore debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash earnings will rise, debt servicing will get easier, and repayment is planned; the company is described as debt-free apart from Netcom acquisition borrowing at about 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Does ResolX/Agentic AI generate savings or margin lift yet?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin benefit is visible in a few projects but is too small to be noticeable yet; deflection to humans is about 30-40%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Singapore acquisition and revenue there?
qa_highlights.answer: The Singapore company acquired in 2025 served as the platform later relaunched as ResolX; there is no current revenue in Singapore, with small revenues in the Middle East, Europe, LATAM and India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended cost of debt, and acquisition criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt sits mainly with Netcom at about 9%. Acquisition screen is EPS accretion first, then North American customer access; management said margin accretion is immediate.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and monetisation of resolution-based model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said resolution cost is measured by time and motion across channels, and that single-owner end-to-end handling shortens interactions (e.g. 5 minutes to 2 minutes).

risks_watch: Margin progression: consolidated EBITDA margin 24.9% is below standalone 30.4%, due to Netcom mix; AI-driven margin uplift is still small.
AI revenue timing: management guided to 12-18 months or longer before AI revenue is meaningful.
Debt of about INR 220 crore at ~9% cost on Netcom acquisition; finance cost rose to INR 8.1 crore.
Management's claim of unique positioning and high 10-12% deal conversion has not been independently verified.
Revenue doubling target for FY27 relies on Netcom consolidation plus new customer ramp-ups.
544748|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the ResolX/Agentic AI narrative and growth trajectory, but vague or evasive on AI-driven margin and revenue quantification, which management repeatedly deferred to future quarters. Some answers on competition and differentiation were assertive without supporting data.
key_quotes: Today, I can say that we are the only ones who exist in India who have the domain plus tech stack plus Agentic AI capabilities, which is truly born within the organization.
We are not in the business of creating LLMs, which is your Large Language Models. What we are in the business is on what sits on top of an LLM.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ResolX launched May 2026 with 12 live deployments across seven clients, 6-7 of 12 deployed; 40-plus bots planned for one Indian insurance client across 7-8 products.

rows.label: Debt repayment on ~INR 220 crore Netcom borrowing
rows.why: Management says cash generation will rise and a repayment schedule is planned on ~INR 220 crore debt at ~9%, against finance cost of INR 8.1 crore in Q1 FY27.

rows.label: Two further acquisitions targeting North American Fortune 500 clients
rows.why: Management intends to acquire two more companies over three years; screen is EPS accretion first, then North American customer access, with no deal named yet.

rows.label: ResolX conversion of active pipeline
rows.why: Management cites 10-12% conversion on active deal pipeline and 12 live deployments across seven enterprise clients, but these figures are unverified and revenue is only starting to catch up.

tone.note: Management was confident on the ResolX/Agentic AI narrative and the revenue-doubling target, but cautious and vague on AI-driven margin and revenue quantification, deferring to later quarters; analysts pushed on the sustainability of the Q1 run rate, Netcom split, and debt servicing.

544750|2026-03.headline: Om Power Transmission Q4 FY26 revenue rose 67.2% YoY to INR 174.62 crores; FY26 order book hit a record INR 621 crores.
544750|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 174.62 crores, up 67.2% YoY and 68% QoQ, with EBITDA margin of 13.10% versus 17.50% a year earlier. FY26 revenue grew 60.7% to INR 449.16 crores, PAT rose 81.2% to INR 40.02 crores, and ROCE was 44%. Year-end unexecuted order book reached a record INR 621 crores (book-to-bill 1.38x), and management guided to roughly 50% growth in FY27. This was the company's maiden earnings call following its April 2026 listing.

financial_highlights.change: vs 17.50% in Q4 FY25 and 12.51% in Q3 FY26
ROCE 44% in both FY26 and FY25

segments.name: Transmission line EPC
segments.commentary: Largest vertical at 51.61% of FY26 revenue; INR 449 crores of the INR 621 crores order book. Company has erected over 1,000 circuit km since incorporation.

segments.name: Substation EPC
segments.commentary: 21.86% of FY26 revenue; INR 140 crores of order book. Covers AIS and GIS up to 220 kV with SCADA monitoring.

segments.name: Underground cabling
segments.commentary: 19.32% of FY26 revenue but only INR 10 crores (about 2%) of order book; management said existing UG projects are executed and a pipeline is building, mainly GETCO tenders.

segments.name: Operation and maintenance
segments.commentary: 7.21% of FY26 revenue; INR 21 crores of order book. Operates more than 100 substations and more than 400 km of transmission lines under long-term contracts.

Sustained EBITDA margin of 12% to 13% and PAT margin of 8% to 9%.

Price variation clauses in almost all POs pass through raw-material price increases; margins differ by project, with specialised pile foundation work carrying separate margin levels.
Management says it pre-orders routine items such as insulators and breakers to manage supply shortages.

qa_highlights.question: How fast will the INR 620 crore order book execute and what FY27 growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution timeline is 12-24 months, averaging about 18 months. CFO said FY27 would match the last three years' performance, i.e. around 50% growth.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling T&D material shortages and price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Materials are ordered as soon as an LOI arrives, and routine items are bulk-booked in advance. Almost all POs have price variation clauses that compensate cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Why has underground cabling share fallen, and is the company deprioritising it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said existing UG projects were completed on time and more UG tenders are in the pipeline, mainly GETCO. Growth is expected from both UG and overhead lines.

qa_highlights.question: Why is private-sector revenue share falling (35% in FY23 to 15-16% in FY25)?
qa_highlights.answer: Company only takes private projects that meet its margin threshold. Overhead transmission is its core business, with 66 kV and above focus.

qa_highlights.question: What are the win ratio, order pipeline and margin expectations for new states?
qa_highlights.answer: Win ratio on the INR 900 crore pipeline is 30-40%. Margins in new states may be somewhat lower, but management expects to win at similar EBITDA. Guidance is 12-13% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the working capital cycle stay around 75 days, and what is retention money?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 80% of RA bills are paid within 30 days, with the balance tied to erection and final completion. Retention of about INR 66 crores was outstanding at March 2026.

Underground cabling order book is only about 2%-3% of the total, against 19% of FY26 revenue.
Entry into 765 kV, distribution and new states carries execution and margin risk, with no current 765 kV orders.
Retention money of about INR 66 crores (March 2026) ties up working capital.

544754|2026-03.headline: Kissht (OnEMI) FY26 AUM rose 73% YoY to ₹7,066 crore; GNPA fell to 2.12% and FY26 PAT grew 75% to ₹281 crore.
544754|2026-03.overview: First earnings call since the May 8, 2026 listing. AUM grew 19% QoQ to ₹7,066 crore and PAT grew 52% YoY and 7% QoQ in Q4. Asset quality improved, with GNPA down 77 bps YoY to 2.12% and Stage-3 ECL coverage at 86.2%. Management deliberately reduced yields to target higher-quality borrowers, which compressed the Q3-to-Q4 margin, and guided to FY27 AUM growth above 40%, ROA of 4.5-5% and ROE of 19-21%.

financial_highlights.metric: Impairment cost as % of average AUM

segments.name: Personal loans (unsecured, on-book and off-book)
segments.commentary: On-book AUM ₹3,556 crore and off-book AUM ₹3,510 crore, with off-book covered by FLDG capped at 5%. Disbursements were cut about 7% and about 450 pin codes were paused on early-warning flags.

segments.name: Loan Against Property (LAP)
segments.commentary: AUM about ₹518 crore across 98 branches in 8 states, or 7.3% of AUM. LTV is about 48% and expected to stay range-bound. LAP is not yet at breakeven and is about 1-2 years from steady-state ROA.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth above 40%, with secured book scale-up expected to be strong.
Gross NPA below 2.25%, impairment costs down 10-15% YoY, and continued Stage-1 mix improvement.
Return on average AUM of 4.5-5%, which implies ROE of 19-21%. Guidance is for FY27 alone.
Yield is expected to keep declining over the next four to six quarters at a pace similar to Q3-to-Q4. Yield minus cost of borrowing is about 18-19% near term and 14-16% in three to four quarters.
Cost of borrowing fell about 200 bps after the Crisil A- upgrade in February 2026; a further upgrade in FY27 could cut it another 100-150 bps in FY28.
LAP: at least 80 more branches by end of FY27, with calibrated expansion in Karnataka, AP, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, UP and Maharashtra.
No disbursement guidance for FY27; guidance is on AUM growth.
capex_capacity: IPO proceeds: 75% of primary issue (about ₹630 crore) already infused as equity into NBFC subsidiary Si Creva Capital; balance 25% for general corporate purposes including technology, AI, brand and customer acquisition.
Capital position described as comfortable for 40% AUM growth in FY27; no near-term fundraise indicated.
Collections team expanded in Q4 FY26, mainly on the field side, with a dedicated NPA recovery team. Operating base: over 7,000 field agents and 1,000+ tele-callers.
Steady-state on-book debt-to-equity seen at 2.5-3x; off-book leverage not a constraint since only the 5% FLDG is blocked.
New wholly-owned subsidiary created to distribute mutual funds and wealth products.
demand_pricing: Margin compression is deliberate: yields reduced to win higher-quality, lower-risk borrowers, with benefits from operating leverage and lower funding costs partly passed to customers.
Repeat customers: 11.76 million unique customers to date, about 3.5 million active; repeat share supports growth.
Acquisition: digital marketing under 50% of acquisition, partner channels (merchants, e-commerce, aggregators) about 55%, organic about 30%.
Competition cited as Bajaj and Chola; management points to credit performance and repeat-customer base as edge.
Borrowing cost on-book ranged 11.5%-14.25% across 45+ lenders.

qa_highlights.question: Rating upgrade outlook and impact on borrowing cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Crisil rated A- in Feb 2026 and India Ratings A- in Nov 2025. About 200 bps lower marginal cost of borrowing already seen since the Crisil upgrade. Another upgrade is possible in FY27 (discussion over next 6-8 months), worth a further 100-150 bps in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is GNPA so much higher than two years ago (0.79% to 2.89%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a technical change: the write-off period was extended from 120 to 150 days after discussion with auditors. GNPA has been stable on the 150-day basis for two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 OPEX rise and other income fall?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP not yet at breakeven and branch additions; plus a one-time Q4 investment in field collections staff for FY27 recoveries. Other income fell sequentially with a small margin compression.

qa_highlights.question: What is the portfolio yield and where does it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 portfolio yield about 30-31%, 50-75 bps below Q3. Management expects a similar downward trend for four to six quarters. Yield minus cost of borrowing is about 18-19% near term.

qa_highlights.question: Is FLDG capped at 5% and can lenders push IRR above it?
qa_highlights.answer: Contractual risk is capped at 5% FLDG. Lenders may negotiate on hurdle rates, but the exposure does not extend beyond the FLDG.

qa_highlights.question: How is AUM growth changing the ROA and secured-mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall AUM growth above 40%. The 4.5% ROA guidance covers the whole book, with secured lending at lower ROA. Management expects secured to reach roughly 19-21% ROE over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LAP and AUM growth accelerate QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeting higher-quality customers at lower rates, plus repeat customers from the 3.5 million active base. Management says April-May momentum continues.

risks_watch: Yield compression is guided to continue for four to six quarters; ROA of 4.5-5% depends on funding-cost and opex offsets.
LAP is loss-making at the margin and needs 1-2 years to reach steady-state ROA; 80 new branches add opex.
Stage-3 and gross NPA trends depend on the 150-day write-off policy; a change in policy would shift the reported number.
Off-book book depends on FLDG partner appetite and on negotiated lender hurdle rates.
Rating upgrade and resulting funding-cost cuts are not assured; timing depends on FY27 rating reviews.
544754|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and guidance, with explicit emphasis on prudence and ROA protection. Cautious on near-term margins, which management openly says will keep declining. Evasive on disbursement targets and on the exact origination yield for April-May.
key_quotes: And at this stage, we believe, Prudence ceases to be a conservative instinct - it becomes a genuine competitive advantage.
We would rather carry prudence slightly early than discover optimism slightly late.
Kissht is a technology company that does lending - not the other way around, a lending company that uses technology.

We are not building for the next quarter, rather, we are building for the next decade - with sharper judgments, stronger governance, deeper technology, and a balance sheet designed to compound through cycles, not merely benefit from favorable ones.

rows.label: Margin expansion

Credit cost fell to 6.80% of average AUM from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26. Management reiterated FY27 guidance (AUM growth of 40%+, 15% credit cost reduction, ROA of 5%+ and ROE of 20%+) and said it is on track.

544754|2026-09.headline: Kissht Q2 FY27: AUM up 68% YoY to Rs 9,317 crore and PAT doubled to Rs 125 crore, with credit cost down to 6.2% of AUM.

Asset quality improved on most measures, with Gross NPA at 2.18%, Stage-2 at 2.37%, and credit cost at 6.2% of average AUM. Cost of borrowing fell to 13.76% from 14.45%. Management raised FY27 AUM growth guidance to 60%+ and impairment reduction guidance to more than 15% YoY, and completed a Rs 832 crore preferential allotment.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost of funds, operating leverage and lower risk cost let it pass part of the benefit to customers while keeping ROA and ROE at past levels plus a cushion. NCD raises were about 150 bps below the 13.76% blended cost.

qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred the fund-use question to the CFO and said committed GPU funding is fully arranged through debt, accruals or past equity; future equity raises would be disclosed when they happen.

risks_watch: Margin sustainability: the 75.2% EBITDA margin relies on utilisation at maximum and a strong pricing environment; management said DC and electricity costs will rise with usage.
Rising debt: the loan for the first B200 lot is ~INR 450 crore and will increase with the next lot; interest cost spiked in the quarter and peak debt was not quantified.
Hardware refresh and pricing risk: management cited short generation cycles and ASIC diversification, and described a 6-year GPU life cycle without much detail on ROIC protection.
Reliance on a few large contracts and India AI mission customers; management declined to disclose customer concentration and the Indian AI Nation commitment status was left open.
Question on the INR881.1 crore capex and use of preferential-issue proceeds was not answered in full.
544783|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand and the sovereign AI thesis, but evasive on specifics: management declined to give MRR guidance, customer mix, peak debt, the SovCloud funding plan and use of preferential-issue funds, and deferred several questions to later updates.
key_quotes: So, we are very focused on building the operating leverage for us on the principle of do less and do better.
We don't provide guidance on MRR.
We will not be quantifying that amount.
And it's still day zero at AI.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin hit 75.2% (up 1,450 bps QoQ) on maximum utilisation and a July price increase, but management said DC and electricity costs will rise with usage and it gave no margin guidance, so the peak may not hold.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The next B200 lot is expected within about two months of the call (Q2 FY27), on top of 1,024 B200s already live since mid-May, against ~5,100 live GPUs.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management said the existing fleet is at maximum utilisation and growth will come mainly from capacity additions, with the next B200 lot due in about two months and 1,024 B200s (~20% of live base) added in Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is at maximum, management said it plans more Blackwell including non-flagship and Vera Rubin, and preliminary planning has started for B300 and Vera Rubin, though no GPU count or timeline is committed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric revenue guidance, but Q1 revenue rose 64% QoQ to INR1,568 million and the next B200 lot adds capacity, so a raised outlook depends on the lot arriving on time.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Debt is about INR 450 crore and rising with the next lot, interest cost spiked in Q1, and some customers were given price holds for 1-2 year contracts, which could compress realisation if utilisation or pricing softens.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans Vera Rubin and non-flagship Blackwell capacity and has started preliminary planning for B300, but gave no timeline or GPU count.

rows.label: July GPU/CPU price increase
rows.why: Most customers are renegotiating after contract expiry with little pushback, but management said growth will come mainly from capacity rather than the hike and gave no quantified impact.

rows.label: Shift to 1-3 year contracts
rows.why: Management intends to move some capacity to 1-3 year contracts (percentage undecided) and offered price holds for 1-2 year contracts or advance payment, which would add revenue visibility but cap pricing upside.

rows.label: Rising debt for B200 lots
rows.why: The loan is about INR 450 crore for the first B200 lot and will rise as the next lot arrives, with management declining to quantify peak debt.

tone.note: Management was confident on utilisation at maximum, the B200 ramp and the sovereign AI thesis, but evasive on MRR guidance, customer mix, peak debt, SovCloud funding and use of preferential-issue proceeds; analysts pressed on margin sustainability, debt and the INR881.1 crore capex.
